```{r setup}
source(here::here("common.R"))

dir26 <- here("data/stories_2026-09")
res_items <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "results_items.rds"))
res_dim   <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "results_dimensionality.rds"))
res_inv   <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "results_invariance.rds"))
res_rel   <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "results_reliability.rds"))
trials    <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "stories_trials.rds"))
runs      <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "stories_runs.rds"))
recon     <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "reconciliation.rds"))

# block-CAT design simulation (tasks/_stories_cat_sim.R)
res_cat <- read_rds(file.path(dir26, "results_cat_sim.rds"))
rule_labels <- c(random = "random", maxinfo = "max information", infomin = "information per minute",
                 rq2 = "top-2 randomesque", disc_a2 = "highest summed discrimination",
                 disc_mean = "highest mean discrimination", oracle = "information at true θ",
                 fixed = "fixed form")
cat_designs <- res_cat$designs |> select(design, design_label = label, n_stories, steps)
# mean realized reliability over the 8 calibration groups; minutes = median over groups
cat_grid <- res_cat$q1 |>
  group_by(design, n_stories, rule) |>
  summarise(rel = mean(rel_realized), med_min = median(median_min), q90_min = median(q90_min),
            max_exp = mean(max_exposure), .groups = "drop")
cg <- function(d, r, col = "rel") {
  x <- cat_grid[[col]][cat_grid$design == d & cat_grid$rule == r]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1); x
}

# number formatting: n2(0.456) = ".46", n2(1.234) = "1.23"
n2  <- function(x, d = 2) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
big <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
rng <- function(x, d = 2) {
  lo <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE); hi <- max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  paste0(n2(lo, d), if (lo < 0) " to " else "–", n2(hi, d))
}
fp  <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)          # tables
pe  <- function(p) if (p < 1e-4) "< .0001" else paste("=", n2(p, 3))  # prose: "p `r pe(x)`"
spct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(if_else(x > 0, "+", ""), pct(x, d))
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
# pull exactly one value out of a results table (fails loudly otherwise)
pick <- function(df, col, ...) {
  x <- dplyr::filter(df, ...) |> dplyr::pull({{ col }})
  if (length(x) != 1) stop("pick(): expected 1 row, got ", length(x))
  x
}

# item labels: "tom_story4_deception_reality_check_2" -> "S4 rc_2"
short_entry <- function(e) e |>
  str_replace("false_belief", "fb") |> str_replace("reality_check", "rc") |>
  str_replace("emotion_reasoning", "er") |> str_replace("^reference", "ref")
uid_label <- function(uid) {
  m <- str_match(uid, paste0("story(\\d+)_(?:reality_known|moral_reasoning|interpretation|",
                             "deception|reference|second_order)_(.+?)(?:-\\d+)?$"))
  paste0("S", m[, 2], " ", short_entry(m[, 3]))
}

# palettes: languages borrow the colour of their main site in common.R's site_pal
lang_levels <- c("de-DE", "en-US", "en-GB", "es-CO", "es-AR")
lang_pal <- c("de-DE" = site_pal[["pilot_mpieva_de"]],
              "en-US" = site_pal[["pilot_western_ca"]],
              "en-GB" = site_pal[["rfp1_sheffield_gb"]],
              "es-CO" = site_pal[["pilot_uniandes_co"]],
              "es-AR" = site_pal[["rfp1_utdt_ar"]])
qtype_levels <- c("false_belief", "emotion_reasoning", "reference", "reality_check")
qtype_pal <- set_names(ptol_pal()(4), qtype_levels)

# dimensionality samples
dim_labels <- c(de_ib = "Leipzig item bank (de-DE)", de_ib_v2 = "Leipzig, V2 content only",
                de_ib_junelike = "Leipzig, June-style rebuild",
                wca_ib = "Western item bank (en-US)", bog_ib = "Bogotá item bank (es-CO)",
                bog_ib_nofb = "Bogotá, without story-1 FB",
                ar_nhb = "UTDT no-HA retest-B (es-AR)", ar_nhb_nofb = "UTDT, without story-13 FB")
dim_primary <- c("de_ib", "wca_ib", "bog_ib", "ar_nhb")
dim_pal <- c(de_ib = site_pal[["pilot_mpieva_de"]], wca_ib = site_pal[["pilot_western_ca"]],
             bog_ib = site_pal[["pilot_uniandes_co"]], ar_nhb = site_pal[["rfp1_utdt_ar"]])

small_groups <- res_rel$meta$small_groups   # < 25 runs: scored under the DE prior

# what PR #27 adds against the releases: restored trials vs mapped trials in newly included runs
k_add <- list(restored = sum(recon$added_by_kind$n[str_starts(recon$added_by_kind$kind, "restored")]),
              mapped = sum(recon$added_by_kind$n[recon$added_by_kind$kind == "mapped before, run newly included"]),
              flip_runs = sum(recon$run_flips$n[recon$run_flips$before == "few_valid_trials" &
                                                 recon$run_flips$after == "included"]))
stopifnot(k_add$restored + k_add$mapped == sum(recon$per_dataset$added))

# story lists as runs of consecutive numbers: c(2, 7:12) -> "2, 7–12"
story_ranges <- function(s) {
  s <- sort(unique(s)); brk <- c(0, which(diff(s) != 1), length(s))
  paste(map_chr(seq_len(length(brk) - 1), \(i) {
    r <- s[(brk[i] + 1):brk[i + 1]]
    if (length(r) > 1) paste0(r[1], "–", r[length(r)]) else as.character(r)
  }), collapse = ", ")
}

# dataset labels (common.R has no label for rfp1_mpib_de_main)
ds_label <- function(d) coalesce(unname(dataset_labels_named[d]), d)
```

# Purpose and what changed since June

This chapter consolidates the Stories (Theory of Mind, ToM) analyses on the
newest data, with item identities corrected. It supersedes three June
chapters, now retired to `old/` in the
[source repository](https://github.com/levante-framework/levante-analysis):
structure, rescoring and item analysis (`old/stories_tom.qmd`),
dimensionality (`old/tom_dimensionality.qmd`) and multigroup DIF
(`old/tom_dif_multigroup.qmd`). The June
[forensic reconstruction](tom_reality_check_bug.qmd) stays as the appendix
on how the early deployment defects were found. The section on the exclusion
list below revises its account of what went wrong with each item.

The June chapters were frozen on 2026-07-16. They used the June v1_2
release (pilot sites only) and the v1_14 per-language scoring models. Since
then, five things have changed:

1. **Data.** Every raw site dataset with ToM runs, pinned on 2026-09-24:
   `r big(n_distinct(trials$run_id))` included runs from
   `r big(n_distinct(trials$user_id))` children, `r big(nrow(trials))`
   trials, `r n_distinct(trials$dataset)` datasets and
   `r n_distinct(trials$language)` languages. The largest new sample is UTDT
   Argentina (es-AR), which runs only stories 13–18.
2. **Item identity.** levantemodels PR #27 (unmerged) fixes item identities
   in three deployment epochs and sets chance per story question. Against the
   latest releases (for Sheffield, its unreleased next draft of 2026-09-24,
   which matches the pinned raw data) it adds `r big(sum(recon$per_dataset$added))`
   trials: `r big(k_add$restored)` restored by PR #27 and `r k_add$mapped` in
   `r k_add$flip_runs` Bogotá runs that the restores lift above the 10-trial
   minimum. It relabels `r big(sum(recon$per_dataset$relabelled))` and changes
   `correct` for `r sum(recon$per_dataset$correct_differs)` trials.
3. **Item policy.** Items are excluded by story-level flags defined in the
   data build (`tasks/_build_stories_data.R`), not by the generic Airtable
   list. The Spanish reality_known false-belief items are a sensitivity set,
   analysed with and without. The flags are listed below; they are analysis
   choices, and the recommendations say where they should live.
4. **Scoring.** Each dataset with at least 25 runs gets its own group mean
   and variance, as proposed in levantemodels PR #26 (unmerged). Here the
   groups are estimated in one concurrent calibration, on a wider integration
   grid than production uses.
5. **Methods.** The reliability and invariance models fix the guessing floor
   at chance (the LEVANTE convention). The dimensionality models set it to 0
   for items answered at or below chance, and the other two analyses are
   rerun under that rule as a check. Correlations are computed within
   dataset × form rather than pooled over sites. Reliability is reported as
   empirical (EAP) reliability of what children actually answered.
   Dimensionality uses a resampled parallel analysis and bifactor models.

Four analysis scripts produced the results this chapter reads (see
[Reproducing](#reproducing)). The chapter itself fits no models.

```{r key-numbers}
k <- list()
fs <- res_items$flag_summary$by_language
k$cells_ok      <- sum(fs$ok)
k$cells_ceiling <- sum(fs$ceiling)
k$cells_weak    <- sum(fs$weak)
k$cells_poor    <- sum(fs$poor)
k$cells_bcd     <- sum(fs$`below chance, discriminating`)
k$cells_flag    <- k$cells_ok + k$cells_ceiling + k$cells_weak + k$cells_poor + k$cells_bcd
k$acc_13_ar <- pick(res_items$items_lang, accuracy,
                    story_uid == "tom_story13_reality_known_false_belief", language == "es-AR")

vc <- res_items$verdict_counts
vcn <- \(v) sum(vc$n[vc$verdict == v])
k$v_es_disc <- vcn("un-exclude (below chance in Spanish, but discriminates)")
k$v_un   <- vcn("un-exclude") + vcn("un-exclude (weak item)") + k$v_es_disc
k$v_weak <- vcn("un-exclude (weak item)")
k$v_es   <- vcn("un-exclude; flag es-* in analyses, no Airtable row until the translation check")
k$v_scop <- vcn("scoped exclusion")
k$v_keep <- vcn("keep excluded")
k$v_all  <- sum(vc$n)
stopifnot(k$v_un + k$v_es + k$v_scop + k$v_keep == k$v_all)

cr <- res_items$construct_r2
k$r2_qt  <- pick(cr, R2, outcome == "difficulty (IRT, z within language)",
                 unit == "item x language", scheme == "question_type (4)")
k$r2_og  <- pick(cr, R2, outcome == "difficulty (IRT, z within language)",
                 unit == "item x language", scheme == "old_group (6)")
k$r2_nc  <- pick(cr, R2, outcome == "difficulty (IRT, z within language)",
                 unit == "item x language", scheme == "new_construct (6)")
slope_unit <- "item x language (language FE; dR2 over it)"
k$dr2_nc <- pick(cr, dR2, outcome == "age slope (logit per year)", unit == slope_unit,
                 scheme == "new_construct (6)")
k$p_nc   <- pick(cr, p, outcome == "age slope (logit per year)", unit == slope_unit,
                 scheme == "new_construct (6)")

eg <- res_dim$eigen
k$ev_de <- pick(eg, ev1_ev2, sample == "de_ib")
k$ev_other <- eg$ev1_ev2[eg$sample %in% setdiff(dim_primary, "de_ib")]
ld <- res_dim$irt_ld |> filter(family == "guess", sample %in% dim_primary)
k$ecv <- rng(ld$ECV); k$omh <- rng(ld$omega_h); k$cor_uni_g <- rng(ld$cor_theta_uni_general, 3)
k$info_over <- paste0(pct(min(ld$info_overstatement)), "–", pct(max(ld$info_overstatement)))
spec_signs <- res_dim$irt_slopes |>
  filter(family == "guess", has_story_factor, sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  group_by(sample, story) |>
  summarise(mixed = any(lambda_specific < 0) & any(lambda_specific > 0),
            sum_abs = sum(abs(lambda_specific)), abs_sum = abs(sum(lambda_specific)), .groups = "drop")
k$mixed_stories <- sum(spec_signs$mixed); k$n_story_factors <- nrow(spec_signs)
k$de_s2_abs <- pick(spec_signs, sum_abs, sample == "de_ib", story == 2)
k$de_s2_sum <- pick(spec_signs, abs_sum, sample == "de_ib", story == 2)

cc <- res_items$controls_cor
k$r_ct_pooled <- pick(cc, r_control_target, method == "pooled over runs (June method)",
                      item_set == "policy items dropped")
k$r_ct_within <- pick(cc, r_control_target, method == "within dataset x form, Fisher-pooled",
                      item_set == "policy items dropped")

dbt <- res_inv$dif_by_type
k$A_ctrl_x2  <- pick(dbt, share_of_s1_X2, analysis == "A", kind == "control")
k$A_ctrl_it  <- pick(dbt, share_of_items, analysis == "A", kind == "control")
k$B_ctrl_x2  <- pick(dbt, share_of_s1_X2, analysis == "B", kind == "control")
tst <- res_inv$tests
k$A_scal_x2df <- pick(tst, X2_df, analysis == "A", comparison == "scalar vs configural", items == "all")
k$B_scal_x2df <- pick(tst, X2_df, analysis == "B", comparison == "scalar vs configural", items == "all")
k$A_part_p <- pick(tst, p, analysis == "A", comparison == "partial scalar vs configural", items == "all")
k$B_part_p <- pick(tst, p, analysis == "B", comparison == "partial scalar vs configural", items == "all")

# reliability headline: aggregate fixed-form and fCAT rows per dataset
agg_forms <- c("fCAT", "all fixed forms", "all forms")
form_types <- res_rel$rel_by_form |> filter(!form %in% agg_forms) |> distinct(dataset, form_type)

  res_rel$rel_by_form |> filter(form %in% c("all fixed forms", "fCAT")),

csv <- \(d, col) pick(cs, {{ col }}, dataset == d)

k$stab_60_hi <- pick(sb, r_hi, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[60,180)", version == "analysis")
```

## Summary

```{r summary-numbers}
# numbers the summary needs from later sections (computed here, where the summary is)
sum_q3 <- res_dim$q3_grouping_contrast |> filter(sample %in% dim_primary, grouping == "question type")
sum_st <- res_items$slope_tests
sum_fl <- \(col) pick(sum_st, {{ col }}, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "question_type")
sum_2pl <- \(a, col) pick(res_inv$tests_2pl, {{ col }}, analysis == a, comparison == "scalar vs metric")
sum_rasch <- \(a, col) pick(res_inv$tests, {{ col }}, analysis == a, comparison == "scalar vs configural", items == "all")
```

- **Item quality.** Of the `r k$cells_flag` item × language cells with at
  least 30 responses, `r k$cells_ok` are fine, `r k$cells_ceiling` are at
  ceiling, `r k$cells_weak` discriminate weakly, `r k$cells_poor` are poor
  and `r k$cells_bcd` are below chance but still discriminate. The poor
  cells are the policy-flagged content plus Spanish reality_known
  false-belief items (story 13 in es-AR: `r n2(k$acc_13_ar, 3)` correct
  with two response options).
- **The exclusion list.** The 12 generic Airtable entries cover
  `r k$v_all` story-level items. `r k$v_un` of them should be un-excluded
  (`r k$v_weak` weak; `r k$v_es_disc` below chance in Spanish but still
  discriminating). `r k$v_scop` need exclusions scoped to one content
  version; for the two on image 4g, a key correction is the alternative, if
  the content team confirms it. `r k$v_keep` should stay excluded
  everywhere: reference_reference in stories 5, 11 and 17, and story 10's
  deception false belief 1, which does not discriminate. Story 13's
  reality_known false belief keeps an analysis flag in Spanish, and any
  Airtable row for it should wait for the translation check. The scoped
  rows cannot be written in today's Airtable schema.
- **What organizes the items.** Question type organizes item difficulty
  (R² `r n2(k$r2_qt, 3)`, against `r n2(k$r2_og, 3)` and `r n2(k$r2_nc, 3)`
  for the two story-construct schemes). Above the guessing floor,
  false-belief targets are more age-sensitive than controls (difference
  `r n2(sum_fl(fb_minus_control), 2)` [`r n2(sum_fl(fb_minus_control_lo), 2)`,
  `r n2(sum_fl(fb_minus_control_hi), 2)`] logits per year), so June's
  "false-belief targets carry the age signal" survives on the
  chance-corrected scale; raw logit slopes do not separate them. The
  clustering of tetrachoric correlations by question type partly reflects
  shared difficulty: on IRT residuals the contrast shrinks to
  `r rng(sum_q3$within_minus_between, 3)`, weak and uneven across
  samples.
- **Dimensionality.** A single score is defensible, most clearly outside
  Leipzig. The Leipzig form's eigenvalue ratio is `r n2(k$ev_de)`, as in
  June (on a partly different item set); the Western, Bogotá and es-AR
  forms are at `r rng(k$ev_other)`. In the bifactor models ECV is `r k$ecv` (below the
  usual .70 in Leipzig and es-AR), and scores barely change
  (r = `r k$cor_uni_g`). Story-level local dependence makes a
  unidimensional model overstate information by `r k$info_over`.
- **Controls.** Keep them. They add reliability and cost almost no age
  validity. Their correlation with targets is `r n2(k$r_ct_within)` within
  dataset × form, lower than the pooled `r n2(k$r_ct_pooled)` that June's
  method gives.
- **Cross-language invariance.** In stories 1–6 (de/en-US/es-CO) the LR
  test rejects scalar invariance (χ²/df `r n2(k$A_scal_x2df, 1)`), but BIC
  does not favour non-invariance under the LEVANTE convention or the 2PL
  (Rasch dBIC `r n2(sum_rasch("A", dBIC), 0)`, 2PL `r n2(sum_2pl("A", dBIC), 0)`);
  it does with a guessing floor of 0 for below-chance items
  (dBIC `r n2(sum_rasch("A_g0", dBIC), 0)`).
  Stories 13–18 (de/es-AR) are non-invariant under both models (dBIC
  `r n2(sum_rasch("B", dBIC), 0)` and `r n2(sum_2pl("B", dBIC), 0)`).
  Whether controls or targets carry more of the DIF depends on the model
  and the design, so June's "controls dominate" is weakened, not simply
  overturned. False-belief items are non-invariant in both analyses, but
  language is confounded with prior exposure (most German children in
  stories 13–18 were on a repeat run), age and site. Two sites that share a
  language differ less (by BIC) and mostly on other items, and German
  children under 9 show the same false-belief DIF, so neither site nor age
  alone explains it.
  Partial scalar models fit, but only as a description.
- **Reliability.** Per administration, reliability is moderate:
  `r k$rel_fixed` per dataset, pooling its fixed forms (single forms
  `r k$rel_forms`), and `r k$rel_fcat` for the deployed fCAT (3 random
  stories, median `r k$fcat_min` minutes). Both are upper bounds. June's
  ".92" was a model-implied value for a `r jp$items_in_model`-item pool that
  no child takes; the same model's reliability for what children answered
  is `r n2(jp$rasch_empirical_rxx_eap, 3)`. In the same children, choosing
  the more informative story per block instead of a random one raises the
  reliability of a 3-story form by a median of
  `r n2(median(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random))` (up to
  `r n2(max(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random))`). German alternate-form stability over 2–6 months is
  `r n2(k$stab_60)` [`r n2(k$stab_60_lo)`, `r n2(k$stab_60_hi)`].
- **Block CAT (simulation).** Choosing the most informative story within today's
  three blocks raises mean reliability from `r n2(cg("cur3", "random"))` to
  `r n2(cg("cur3", "maxinfo"))` in the same time; adding a fourth, free story
  reaches `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo"))` in about `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo", "med_min"), 1)`
  median minutes, more than a fixed six-story form in less time. Select by information at
  the current estimate (not by discrimination), under the group's prior; see
  [Designing the block CAT](#designing-the-block-cat).
- **Scoring.** The means and variances of low-scoring groups are weakly
  identified: they move with the integration grid, the latent density and
  the guessing convention, while scores within a group barely change.
  Datasets without their own group in v2_3 were scored under the German
  prior; with their own prior, their level drops by `r k$shift_prior`
  logits.

# Data and provenance

```{r provenance}
prov <- attr(trials, "provenance")
prov$raw_sources |>
  left_join(prov$release_refs, by = "dataset") |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pinned raw datasets (read) and the latest processed releases (for reconciliation only)")
```

- **Build.** `tasks/_build_stories_data.R` ran `process_trials()` with
  levantemodels from the PR #27 branch (`fix-tom-identity-corrections`,
  commit `r substr(prov$levantemodels[["commit"]], 1, 7)`, which sits
  directly on main `bd24157`). On 2026-09-24, `git ls-remote` gave
  `bd24157` for origin/main (the same as the local main) and `3dc148b`
  for `refs/pull/27/head`. Item identity metadata:
  `r prov$metadata[["ref"]]`.
- **Run and trial rules.** These are the production rules the latest
  releases were built with: `r prov$rules[["run"]]`; trials: `r prov$rules[["trial"]]`;
  then `r prov$rules[["run_after_trials"]]`.
- **Reconciliation.** Without PR #27 the rebuild reproduces the releases
  trial for trial (`r recon$pre_vs_release[["pre_not_in_release"]]` rebuilt
  trials missing from the releases, and
  `r recon$pre_vs_release[["release_not_in_pre"]]` the other way round).
  For Sheffield the comparison is with its unreleased next draft of
  2026-09-24 (`:next` in the table above), because its latest release
  (v3_1) predates the pinned raw data. The table below shows what PR #27
  adds.
- **The fCAT is not adaptive.** The `theory-of-mind-item-bank-cat-test`
  corpus ("fCAT") shows one random story from each of 3 story groups. It
  has no item parameters and makes no θ updates. It is analysed here as a
  random 3-story form (`fcat_random3`).

```{r inventory}
trials |>
  group_by(dataset, form, language) |>
  summarise(runs = n_distinct(run_id), children = n_distinct(user_id),
            trials = n(), median_age = median(age[!duplicated(run_id)], na.rm = TRUE),
            stories = story_ranges(story),
            first = as.Date(min(time_started)), last = as.Date(max(time_started)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Included runs by dataset × form × language")
```

```{r pr27}
recon$per_dataset |>
  select(dataset, release_trials, stories_trials, added, relabelled,
         correct_differs, release_runs, stories_runs) |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "What PR #27 changes against the latest releases (trials and runs)")
```

## Item-policy flags

The analyses drop the `policy_exclude` trials by default and analyse the
`spanish_fb_flag` trials both with and without. Neither flag removes rows
from the data file.

```{r policy}
trials |>
  filter(policy_exclude | spanish_fb_flag) |>
  mutate(flag = if_else(policy_exclude, policy_reason,
                        "Spanish reality_known false belief: analyse with and without")) |>
  group_by(flag, item = uid_label(story_uid), item_original) |>
  summarise(trials = n(), datasets = n_distinct(dataset),
            accuracy = mean(correct), chance = first(chance), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(flag, item) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Item-policy flags: trials, content code and accuracy")
```

## Western's empty item-bank runs

```{r western}
wca_empty <- runs |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_western_ca_main", variant_id == "Qx8XB8ZAFwP0RhhiEKw5",
         time_started >= as.POSIXct("2026-04-25", tz = "UTC"), n_trials_raw == 0)
wca_other <- runs |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_western_ca_main", included,
         user_id %in% wca_empty$user_id)
```

`r nrow(wca_empty)` Western runs on the item-bank variant
(`Qx8XB8ZAFwP0RhhiEKw5`) between `r as.Date(min(wca_empty$time_started))`
and `r as.Date(max(wca_empty$time_started))` logged no trials
(`r sum(wca_empty$stop_reason %in% "taskAbort")` with `stop_reason =
taskAbort`). They are excluded as `no_data`. `r n_distinct(wca_other$user_id)`
of the `r n_distinct(wca_empty$user_id)` children involved have an included
ToM run (at any time) in these data. According to the engineering team's
follow-up, no collected data were lost. The variant still
loaded the item-bank corpus, whose hostile-attribution prompts are missing
from the English item-bank translation, so the task failed its startup
corpus check and aborted before the first trial. The children completed the
other tasks. The failure was written up in an internal incident report on 12 July,
logged by error monitoring on 19 and 28 August, and is related to
core-tasks#437 (open since 8 April). The engineering team believes the
variant has since been updated; the last run on it in these data started on
`r as.Date(max(runs$time_started[runs$variant_id %in% "Qx8XB8ZAFwP0RhhiEKw5"]))`,
which fits an update but does not prove one.
Engineering plans a nightly check of open assignments that
reference stale (unregistered) variants and, in the longer term, moving
existing assignments to new variants when an old one is deprecated. For this
chapter, these are missing administrations, not dropped data.

# Item quality and the exclusion list

## Item screen

Each story item was screened in each language with at least 30 responses:
accuracy against chance (exact binomial tests) and item-rest correlation.
The item-rest r is computed within dataset × form and then Fisher-pooled.
The flag levels are *poor* (below chance without credible discrimination,
or item-rest r reliably negative), *below chance but discriminating*,
*ceiling* (≥ .95), *weak* (not above chance, or item-rest r with a 95% CI
upper bound below .20) and *ok*.[^flagrules]

[^flagrules]: The flag rules were revised once after the first run. The
original weak-item rule (item-rest r point estimate < .10) mostly flagged
small fCAT cells, whose item-rest CIs are wide. The revised rule uses the
CI upper bound, checks ceiling before weak, and gives below-chance items
with a credibly positive r their own level. The original criterion is kept
in `r_ir_below_10`; it would flag
`r sum(res_items$items_lang$r_ir_below_10[res_items$items_lang$flag != "n < 30"], na.rm = TRUE)`
of the `r k$cells_flag` cells.

```{r flag-table}
res_items$flag_summary$by_language |>
  select(language, ok, ceiling, weak, `below chance, discriminating`, poor, `n < 30`) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Item × language cells by flag (n ≥ 30 to be flagged)")
```

```{r fig-items, fig.height=13}
il <- res_items$items_lang |>
  filter(flag != "n < 30") |>
  mutate(label = uid_label(story_uid),
         label = paste0(label, case_when(content == "other content" ~ " [other content]",
                                         str_detect(content, "4g") ~ " [4g]",
                                         str_detect(content, "2e") ~ " [2e]",
                                         TRUE ~ "")),
         label = fct_reorder(label, -story),
         question_type = factor(question_type, qtype_levels),
         language = factor(language, lang_levels),
         flag = fct_drop(flag))
ggplot(il, aes(x = accuracy - chance, y = label, colour = language, shape = flag)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = .8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(question_type), scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = lang_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(ok = 16, ceiling = 17, weak = 1,
                                `below chance, discriminating` = 4, poor = 8), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Accuracy minus chance", y = NULL,
       title = "Item accuracy above chance, by language",
       subtitle = "Cells with n ≥ 30; [4g], [2e] and [other content] split the policy-flagged content from the rest") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r poor-not-policy}
res_items$flag_summary$poor_not_policy |>
  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), language, n, accuracy, chance,
            p_below = fp(p_below), r_ir, r_ir_lo, flag, datasets) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Below-chance cells outside the policy flags")
```

```{r items-numbers}
ia <- function(uid, cont = "all", col = accuracy)
  pick(res_items$items_all, {{ col }}, story_uid == uid, content == cont)
il_acc <- function(uid, lang, col = accuracy)
  pick(res_items$items_lang, {{ col }}, story_uid == uid, language == lang, content == "all")
k$s14_ar    <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR")
k$s14_ar_n  <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR", n)
k$s14_ar_r  <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR", r_ir)
k$s14_ar_lo <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR", r_ir_lo)
k$s14_ar_hi <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR", r_ir_hi)
k$s14_ar_age <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "es-AR", median_age)
k$s14_de    <- il_acc("tom_story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "de-DE")
rk_band <- \(uid, lang, band) pick(res_items$rk_fb_age, accuracy, story_uid == uid, language == lang,
                                   age_band == band)
rk_am <- res_items$rk_fb_age_matched
```

What the screen shows:

- Outside the policy flags, the below-chance cells are Spanish false-belief
  items, above all the reality_known question ("where will X look first?")
  of stories 1, 7 and 13. They are not alike. Story 1 in es-CO is below
  chance but discriminates (item-rest r
  `r n2(il_acc("tom_story1_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir))`
  [`r n2(il_acc("tom_story1_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir_lo))`,
  `r n2(il_acc("tom_story1_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir_hi))`]),
  the pattern of children who answer with the object's real location. Story
  7 in es-CO has a similar r
  (`r n2(il_acc("tom_story7_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir))`
  [`r n2(il_acc("tom_story7_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir_lo))`,
  `r n2(il_acc("tom_story7_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", r_ir_hi))`],
  n = `r il_acc("tom_story7_reality_known_false_belief", "es-CO", n)`) and is
  flagged poor only because its interval reaches 0. Story 13 in es-AR carries
  no information: `r n2(k$acc_13_ar, 3)` correct, item-rest r
  `r n2(il_acc("tom_story13_reality_known_false_belief", "es-AR", r_ir), 3)`.
- The failure is not specific to Spanish. Young en-US children are also
  below chance on story 1 (`r n2(rk_band("tom_story1_reality_known_false_belief", "en-US", "<6"))`
  under 6 and `r n2(rk_band("tom_story1_reality_known_false_belief", "en-US", "6-7"))`
  at 6–7 years), and story 13 is at chance in en-GB
  (`r n2(il_acc("tom_story13_reality_known_false_belief", "en-GB"))`,
  n = `r il_acc("tom_story13_reality_known_false_belief", "en-GB", n)`). The
  items "work" only in the older German samples. Compared at the same age,
  though, Spanish-speaking children still answer them less often correctly
  (table below): the Spanish gap is `r rng(-rk_am$es_logit, 1)` logits.
  Age, language, site and sample are confounded, and nobody has checked the
  translation files yet.

```{r fig-rkfb, fig.height=3.8}
res_items$rk_fb_age |>
  filter(n >= 10) |>
  mutate(item = paste0("Story ", story, " reality_known false belief"),
         language = factor(language, lang_levels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_band, accuracy, colour = language, group = language)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = chance), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(item), nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = lang_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age band (years)", y = "Accuracy",
       title = "The reality_known false-belief items by age band and language (cells with n ≥ 10; dashed = chance)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
rk_am |>
  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), ages = paste0(n2(age_lo, 1), "–", n2(age_hi, 1)),
            n_es, n_other, other_languages, spanish_logit = es_logit, lo = es_lo, hi = es_hi,
            acc_at_7_other, acc_at_7_es) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Age-matched comparison: glm(correct ~ age + Spanish) on the ages both groups cover (the intersection of each group's 5th–95th age percentiles)")
```

- The problem reaches beyond stories 1/7/13. Story 14's
  moral-reasoning false belief ("where will he look first for his soccer
  ball?") is below chance in es-AR (`r n2(k$s14_ar, 3)`,
  n = `r big(k$s14_ar_n)`; de-DE `r n2(k$s14_de, 3)`), yet its item-rest r
  is positive (`r n2(k$s14_ar_r, 3)` [`r n2(k$s14_ar_lo, 3)`,
  `r n2(k$s14_ar_hi, 3)`]). That pattern fits young children (median age
  `r n2(k$s14_ar_age, 1)`) who answer with the real location, not a broken
  key. Age and language are confounded here: the es-AR samples are the
  youngest.
- The weakest items outside the policy flags are yes/no "Is [sibling] mad at
  [sibling]?" questions in the parallel deception stories 4 and 16. They sit at or
  near chance everywhere. Two other targets barely discriminate, and story
  10's deception false belief 1 does not discriminate at all (it is now
  policy-excluded; see the verdicts):

```{r weak-targets}
weak_uids <- c("tom_story4_deception_false_belief_3", "tom_story16_deception_reference_2",
               "tom_story16_deception_reference_5", "tom_story10_deception_false_belief_1",
               "tom_story17_reference_emotion_reasoning_1")
res_items$items_all |>
  filter(story_uid %in% weak_uids, content == "all") |>
  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), prompt, n, accuracy, chance,
            r_ir, r_ir_lo, r_ir_hi, lang_weak) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Candidates for item revision (not proposed exclusions)")
```

## The exclusion list, story by story

The Airtable exclusion table holds 12 generic ToM uids, such as
`tom_deception_reality_check_2`. Each names a question type in a story type,
so it applies to all parallel stories. The 2026-09 audit found that none of
them takes effect in the current pipeline: the scoring prep runs its
`anti_join` after `recode_tom()` has rewritten every uid to story level, so
the generic uids match nothing. The table below judges each of the
`r k$v_all` story-level items they cover on the corrected data. `accuracy_kept`
and `r_ir_kept` are the values once the proposed scoped exclusion is
applied.

The verdicts are a check of the data build's policy flags, which were set
from the 2026-09 audit, against the item-screen rules above. For the
"keep excluded" and plain "un-exclude" rows the agreement column is true by
construction. The informative checks are the scoped rows (is the flagged
content below chance while the rest is fine?) and the Spanish rows.

```{r verdicts}
res_items$item_verdicts |>
  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), n_all, accuracy_all, chance_all, r_ir_all,
            accuracy_kept, r_ir_kept, verdict, scope) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Verdicts for the 28 story-level items behind the 12 generic exclusion uids")
```

```{r verdict-counts}
res_items$verdict_counts |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Verdict counts (and agreement with the build's policy flags; true by construction except for the scoped and Spanish rows)")
```

```{r b-numbers}
k$rr5  <- ia("tom_story5_reference_reference")
k$rr11 <- ia("tom_story11_reference_reference")
k$rr17 <- ia("tom_story17_reference_reference")
k$rr5_de <- il_acc("tom_story5_reference_reference", "de-DE")
k$rr5_de_n <- il_acc("tom_story5_reference_reference", "de-DE", n)
k$s4rc2_4g <- ia("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_2", "policy-flagged (4g)")
k$s4rc3_4g <- ia("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_3", "policy-flagged (4g)")
k$s4rc2_4d <- ia("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_2", "other content")
k$s4rc3_4d <- ia("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_3", "other content")
k$s2rc1_2e <- ia("tom_story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_1", "policy-flagged (2e)")
k$s2rc1_2e_n <- ia("tom_story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_1", "policy-flagged (2e)", n)
k$s2rc1_oth <- ia("tom_story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_1", "other content")
# story-4 rc_2 on 4g by language, and the 4d level by language
s4 <- \(uid, cont, lang, col = accuracy)
  pick(res_items$items_lang, {{ col }}, story_uid == uid, content == cont, language == lang)
rc2 <- "tom_story4_deception_reality_check_2"
k$rc2_4d_rng <- rng(res_items$items_lang$accuracy[res_items$items_lang$story_uid == rc2 &
                                                   res_items$items_lang$content == "other content"])
# flipped keys (pooled over languages)
fc <- \(uid, part, col) pick(res_items$flip_check, {{ col }}, story_uid == uid, content_part == part,
                             language == "all")
flip_ci <- \(uid, part) paste0(n2(fc(uid, part, r_ir_flipped)), " [", n2(fc(uid, part, r_ir_flipped_lo)),
                               ", ", n2(fc(uid, part, r_ir_flipped_hi)), "]")
s2r <- \(e, cont, resp) pick(res_items$story2_rc_responses, share, entry == e, content == cont,
                             response == resp)
rl <- res_items$reliability
k$ar13_with <- pick(rl, empirical_rxx, sample == "UTDT-AR main, no-HA retest-B form (stories 13-18)",
                    items == "all items", model == "2PL")
k$ar13_without <- pick(rl, empirical_rxx,
                       sample == "UTDT-AR main, no-HA retest-B form, without the flagged es false-belief item",
                       items == "all items", model == "2PL")
```

What the verdicts say:

- **Keep excluded:** reference_reference in stories 5, 11 and 17
  (`r n2(k$rr5, 3)`, `r n2(k$rr11, 3)` and `r n2(k$rr17, 3)` correct;
  chance .33). It is below chance in every language (cells with at least
  30 responses) except German story 5, which is at chance (`r n2(k$rr5_de, 3)`, n = `r k$rr5_de_n`), and its
  item-rest r is negative in every story. The audit found that children pick
  the literal referent, so a key flip would only duplicate the reality check.
  This is a design problem, and the items are still deployed. Story 10's
  deception false belief 1 also stays excluded: its item-rest r is
  `r n2(pick(res_items$item_verdicts, r_ir_all, story_uid == "tom_story10_deception_false_belief_1"))`
  [`r n2(pick(res_items$item_verdicts, r_ir_lo_all, story_uid == "tom_story10_deception_false_belief_1"))`,
  `r n2(pick(res_items$item_verdicts, r_ir_hi_all, story_uid == "tom_story10_deception_false_belief_1"))`]
  (n = `r pick(res_items$item_verdicts, n_all, story_uid == "tom_story10_deception_false_belief_1")`),
  and its interval spans 0 in every language. The same generic uid covers
  stories 4 and 16, which discriminate and are un-excluded.
- **Scoped: story 4 on image 4g.** Reality check 3 on image 4g
  (`r n2(k$s4rc3_4g, 3)`) is below chance in every language. Reality check 2
  (`r n2(k$s4rc2_4g, 3)`) is below chance in de-DE and en-US, weak in en-GB
  (`r n2(s4(rc2, "policy-flagged (4g)", "en-GB"), 3)`, n =
  `r s4(rc2, "policy-flagged (4g)", "en-GB", n)`, one-sided p =
  `r n2(s4(rc2, "policy-flagged (4g)", "en-GB", p_below), 3)`) and at chance in
  es-CO (`r n2(s4(rc2, "policy-flagged (4g)", "es-CO"), 3)`), still well below
  its level on the earlier image 4d (`r k$rc2_4d_rng`). On 4d both questions
  work, although reality check 3 is weak there too (`r n2(k$s4rc3_4d, 3)` on
  two options). Both are keyed "yes" ("Is Mother/Joshua mad at Isabel
  now?"), but the audit found that image 4g shows Mother, Isabel and Joshua
  smiling, and the story never says that Mother learns what Isabel did. With
  the key flipped to "no", the 4g items score
  `r n2(fc(rc2, "flagged: 4g", accuracy_flipped), 2)` and
  `r n2(fc("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_3", "flagged: 4g", accuracy_flipped), 2)`,
  with item-rest r `r flip_ci(rc2, "flagged: 4g")` and
  `r flip_ci("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_3", "flagged: 4g")`:
  positive but weak (reality check 2's interval only just clears 0), a
  third to a half of the 4d values
  (`r n2(fc(rc2, "other content: 4d", r_ir))` and
  `r n2(fc("tom_story4_deception_reality_check_3", "other content: 4d", r_ir))`).
  The data are consistent with a key that conflicts with the scene. A
  scoped correction (re-key 4g to "no") is therefore the preferred option,
  because it keeps the
  `r big(sum(res_items$flip_check$n[res_items$flip_check$content_part == "flagged: 4g" & res_items$flip_check$language == "all"]))`
  trials, but only once the content team confirms that "no" is right for
  the 4g scene; exclusion is the fallback. This chapter keeps the exclusion
  until then.
- **Scoped: story 2 on the V0 Bogotá content.** Reality check 1 on the
  first Bogotá content (2e, May–June 2024) is `r n2(k$s2rc1_2e, 3)`
  (n = `r k$s2rc1_2e_n`) but `r n2(k$s2rc1_oth, 3)` on later content. The
  V0 pattern is the mirror image of the later one:
  `r pct(s2r("reality_check_1", "V0 Bogota (2e)", "coats"))` of V0 children
  chose "coats" (key "shelf"), and
  `r pct(s2r("reality_check_1", "later content", "shelf"))` later chose
  "shelf". A flipped key would give `r n2(fc("tom_story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_1", "flagged: 2e", accuracy_flipped), 3)`,
  with item-rest r `r flip_ci("tom_story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_1", "flagged: 2e")`.
  The mechanism is undetermined: an inverted key, a question identity
  swapped in the retroactive V0 map, or the V0 content itself. A clean swap
  of the two reality checks is not supported: the paired reality check 2
  (key "coats") drew "coats" from
  `r pct(s2r("reality_check_2", "V0 Bogota (2e)", "coats"))` of V0 children
  and `r pct(s2r("reality_check_2", "later content", "coats"))` later. No V0
  corpus survives to settle it. The scoped exclusion is the conservative
  choice; a key or identity correction is the alternative if the V0 content
  can be recovered.
- **Spanish reality_known false belief.** Stories 1 and 7 still
  discriminate in es-CO (above), so they are un-excluded without a language
  flag. Story 13 does not discriminate in es-AR or es-CO and stays below the
  other languages at matched age; it keeps the analysis flag, but no Airtable
  row is proposed until the translation check. In es-AR it adds nothing to
  the UTDT form: reliability is `r n2(k$ar13_with, 3)` with it and
  `r n2(k$ar13_without, 3)` without it (2PL + guessing, empirical). The
  build's `spanish_fb_flag`, which the analyses run with and without,
  still covers all three stories.
- **Un-exclude:** the other `r k$v_un - k$v_es_disc` items behave normally;
  of these, story 14's moral reality check 1 is weak.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The scoped rows under a flipped key, and story 2's reality checks in V0

```{r flip-check}
res_items$flip_check |>
  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), content_part, language, n, accuracy, accuracy_flipped,
            r_ir, r_ir_lo, r_ir_hi, r_ir_flipped, r_ir_flipped_lo, r_ir_flipped_hi) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Accuracy and item-rest r (within dataset × form, Fisher-pooled) with the deployed and the flipped key")
res_items$story2_rc_responses |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Story 2's two reality checks: which option children chose, V0 Bogotá vs later content (DE trials with hostile-attribution answer strings omitted)")
```
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## What this means for the Airtable exclusion table

The DCC's plan is to keep exclusions in the Airtable
table, so they are documented outside code rather than written into
levantemodels. The verdicts above fit that plan, with three changes:

1. Rows need to be **story-level** (for example
   `tom_story17_reference_reference`), not generic. The four keep-excluded
   rows fit today's columns (`item_uid`, `exclude`, `dataset`).
2. Three rows need a **content scope** that those columns cannot express:
   story-4 reality checks 2 and 3 on image 4g, and story-2 reality check 1
   on the V0 content (2e before 2024-07-01), that is, two content scopes
   covering three items. The table would need a content-version (or
   date-window) column. The 4g rows could instead become a key correction,
   which would need a place of its own (see recommendation 2).
3. **No language-scoped rows yet.** Stories 1 and 7 discriminate in Spanish.
   Story 13 should wait for the translation check; if it then needs a
   Spanish row, the table would also need a language column.

The `policy_exclude` and `spanish_fb_flag` flags this chapter uses are
defined in `tasks/_build_stories_data.R`. They stand in for those rows until
the table can hold them.
:::

```{r airtable-rows}
res_items$item_verdicts |>

  transmute(item = uid_label(story_uid), verdict, proposed_airtable_row) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = glue("Proposed story-level rows other than plain un-exclusions (the other {k$v_un - k$v_es_disc} items only need their generic rows removed)"))
```

# What organizes the items

## Difficulty and age sensitivity

Item difficulty comes from a per-language Rasch model with guessing fixed at
chance, z-scored within language. Age slopes come from item × language
logistic regressions of correctness on age with dataset fixed effects. A
slope needs n ≥ 50 and at least 10 correct and 10 incorrect answers.[^minority]
The R² F-tests on item × language cells treat the cells as independent,
although the same item appears in several languages. The item-level rows
(one value per item, averaged over languages) and the random-effects tests
in the next section do not, and the text leads with them.

[^minority]: The minority rule (≥ 10 correct and ≥ 10 incorrect) was added
after the first run, where one near-ceiling item gave a separated slope of
−170. That slope dominated the R² values. Because of the rule, control
slopes come only from samples where controls are not at ceiling. Unfiltered
slopes are kept in `age_slope_raw`.

```{r construct-r2}
res_items$construct_r2 |>
  filter(outcome %in% c("difficulty (IRT, z within language)", "age slope (logit per year)")) |>
  transmute(outcome, unit, scheme, n_items, R2, dR2, p = fp(p)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Variance in item difficulty and item age slope explained by each scheme (for age slopes on cells, dR2 is over language; cell-level p-values treat cells as independent)")
```

```{r fig-schemes, fig.height=6.5}
sm <- res_items$scheme_means |>
  mutate(scheme = recode(scheme, question_type = "Question type", old_group = "Story type (old)",
                         new_construct = "Construct (new)"),
         scheme = factor(scheme, c("Question type", "Story type (old)", "Construct (new)")))
p_slope <- ggplot(sm, aes(x = mean_age_slope, y = fct_reorder(level, mean_age_slope))) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = mean_age_slope - se_age_slope, xmax = mean_age_slope + se_age_slope)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scheme), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Raw age slope (logit/yr, ± SE)", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_blank())
p_diff <- ggplot(sm, aes(x = mean_difficulty_z, y = fct_reorder(level, mean_age_slope))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scheme), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Difficulty (z within language)", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
patchwork::wrap_plots(p_slope, p_diff, nrow = 1) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Question type orders difficulty; raw age slopes (no guessing floor) barely differ")
```

```{r qtype-summary}
res_items$qtype_summary |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "By question type (item × language cells; raw logit age slopes)")
```

```{r slope-numbers}
st <- res_items$slope_tests
spq <- res_items$slope_by_qtype |> filter(filter == "symmetric (floor model)")
k$fl_fb   <- pick(spq, mean_slope_floor, question_type == "false_belief")
k$fl_rc   <- pick(spq, mean_slope_floor, question_type == "reality_check")
k$ame_fb  <- pick(spq, mean_ame_floor, question_type == "false_belief")
k$ame_rc  <- pick(spq, mean_ame_floor, question_type == "reality_check")
k$fl_diff <- pick(st, fb_minus_control, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "question_type")
k$fl_lo   <- pick(st, fb_minus_control_lo, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "question_type")
k$fl_hi   <- pick(st, fb_minus_control_hi, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "question_type")
k$fl_p    <- pick(st, p, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "question_type")
k$raw_diff <- pick(st, fb_minus_control, outcome == "age_slope", scheme == "question_type")
k$raw_lo   <- pick(st, fb_minus_control_lo, outcome == "age_slope", scheme == "question_type")
k$raw_hi   <- pick(st, fb_minus_control_hi, outcome == "age_slope", scheme == "question_type")
k$raw_p    <- pick(st, p, outcome == "age_slope", scheme == "question_type")
k$nc_raw_p <- pick(st, p, outcome == "age_slope", scheme == "new_construct")
k$nc_fl_p  <- pick(st, p, outcome == "slope_floor", scheme == "new_construct")
ib <- \(sch, col) pick(cr, {{ col }}, outcome == "age slope (logit per year)", unit == "item (mean over languages)",
                       scheme == sch)
isl <- res_rel$item_slopes_by_type
k$a_fb <- pick(isl, median_a, question_type == "false_belief")
k$a_rc <- pick(isl, median_a, question_type == "reality_check")
asf <- res_items$age_slopes_floor
k$n_floor_fail <- sum(is.na(asf$slope_floor) & asf$cc_accuracy >= .1 & asf$cc_accuracy <= .9)
```

- **Difficulty is question type.** Question type explains
  `r n2(pick(cr, R2, outcome == "difficulty (IRT, z within language)", unit == "item (mean over languages)", scheme == "question_type (4)"))`
  of the variance across items (`r n2(k$r2_qt)` across item × language
  cells); control vs target alone explains
  `r n2(pick(cr, R2, outcome == "difficulty (IRT, z within language)", unit == "item x language", scheme == "control vs target (2)"))`
  across cells. Either construct scheme explains about `r n2(k$r2_og, 2)`.
  Reference and false-belief questions are hard and reality checks easy.
  June found the same.
- **Raw age slopes barely differ by question type.** Across items, question
  type explains R² = `r n2(ib("question_type (4)", R2), 3)` of the raw
  slopes (p = `r n2(ib("question_type (4)", p), 2)`), and a random-effects
  comparison puts false belief minus controls at `r n2(k$raw_diff, 3)`
  [`r n2(k$raw_lo, 3)`, `r n2(k$raw_hi, 3)`] logits per year. But raw
  slopes ignore the guessing floor, and their filter drops ceiling cells
  while keeping cells near the floor, which flattens false-belief slopes.
  The next section corrects both.
- The new construct scheme's cell-level test (ΔR² = `r n2(k$dr2_nc, 3)`,
  p = `r n2(k$p_nc, 3)`) does not hold up with item random effects
  (p = `r n2(k$nc_raw_p, 2)` for raw slopes, `r n2(k$nc_fl_p, 2)` above the
  floor).
- Dropping the Spanish reality_known false-belief items changes none of
  this (see the sensitivity table below).

### Age sensitivity above the guessing floor

Each item × language cell is refitted with the floor fixed at chance,
P = c + (1 − c) · logistic(a + b · age), by maximum likelihood. Cells are
kept symmetrically: chance-corrected accuracy between .10 and .90, n ≥ 50,
SE(b) ≤ 1 (`r k$n_floor_fail` cells in that range did not converge). The
probability-scale slope is the average marginal effect over the cell's
children. Question types are compared with a random-effects
meta-regression with crossed item and language intercepts
(`metafor::rma.mv`).

```{r floor-slopes}
res_items$slope_by_qtype |>
  select(filter, question_type, n_cells, n_items, mean_accuracy, mean_slope_logit, mean_slope_floor,
         mean_ame_logit, mean_ame_floor) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Age slopes by question type: raw logit, above the floor, and on the probability scale (per year), under the original and the symmetric filter")
res_items$slope_tests |>
  mutate(p = fp(p)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Random-effects tests (items and languages as crossed random intercepts; fb_minus_control from REML, 95% CI)")
```

- **Above the floor, false-belief targets are the most age-sensitive
  items.** Their slope is `r n2(k$fl_fb, 3)` logits per year against
  `r n2(k$fl_rc, 3)` for controls; the difference is `r n2(k$fl_diff, 3)`
  [`r n2(k$fl_lo, 3)`, `r n2(k$fl_hi, 3)`], and question type matters
  (p = `r n2(k$fl_p, 3)`). On the probability scale, false-belief accuracy
  rises by `r n2(k$ame_fb, 3)` per year against `r n2(k$ame_rc, 3)` for
  controls. The 2PL of the reliability model agrees: the median
  false-belief slope is `r n2(k$a_fb)`, against `r n2(k$a_rc)` for controls.
- So June's "false-belief targets carry the age signal" survives, on the
  chance-corrected scale. On raw logits the two cannot be told apart, and
  controls also look flat because many are at ceiling.

## Dimensionality

The factor-analytic samples are complete fixed forms, one run per child,
with policy items dropped. Following June, items need coverage > .4 and
.08 < p < .97. Leipzig is the June sample. Western and Bogotá give the same
stories in other languages, and the UTDT no-HA retest-B form gives
`r big(pick(res_dim$samples, children, sample == "ar_nhb"))` es-AR children
on stories 13–18.

```{r dim-samples}
res_dim$samples |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], role, language, stories, datasets, runs, children,
            items, age = paste0(age_min, "–", age_max, " (median ", age_median, ")"),
            n_age, first_run, last_run) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dimensionality samples")
```


```{r dim-eigen}
res_dim$eigen |>

  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Eigenvalues of the tetrachoric matrix. ev1_ev2_se is a bootstrap SE (200 person resamples). pa_june_nfact uses June's parallel analysis; pa_resample_nfact (factors) and pa_resample_ncomp (components) compare against column-resampled binary data (20 draws).")
```

```{r fig-scree, fig.height=5}
res_dim$scree |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary, component <= 10) |>
  mutate(sample = factor(dim_labels[sample], dim_labels[dim_primary])) |>
  pivot_longer(c(eigenvalue, pa_resampled_pc), names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(series = recode(series, eigenvalue = "observed",
                         pa_resampled_pc = "resampled-data reference")) |>
  ggplot(aes(component, value, linetype = series)) +
```
