- The Leipzig item-bank form's ev1/ev2 (`r n2(k$ev_de)`, on
  `r pick(res_dim$eigen, n_items, sample == "de_ib")` items) is close to
  June's 1.90 on 26 items; the June-style rebuild gives
  `r n2(pick(res_dim$eigen, ev1_ev2, sample == "de_ib_junelike"))`. The
  Western, Bogotá and es-AR forms are at
  `r rng(k$ev_other)`. Leipzig is near ceiling: its items average
  p = `r n2(mean(res_dim$item_info$p[res_dim$item_info$sample == "de_ib" & res_dim$item_info$kept]))`,
  and `r sum(res_dim$item_info$p[res_dim$item_info$sample == "de_ib" & res_dim$item_info$kept] > .9)`
  of its `r pick(res_dim$eigen, n_items, sample == "de_ib")` kept items
  exceed .90. Ceiling is a likely cause of the low ratio but not a tested
  one: the samples also differ in stories, language and age.
- June's parallel-analysis method gives
  `r rng(res_dim$eigen$pa_june_nfact, 0)` factors in every sample, as it
  gave June 11. Against resampled binary data, the primary samples need
  `r rng(res_dim$eigen$pa_resample_ncomp[res_dim$eigen$sample %in% dim_primary], 0)`
  components but `r rng(res_dim$eigen$pa_resample_nfact[res_dim$eigen$sample %in% dim_primary], 0)`
  factors (es-AR:
  `r pick(res_dim$eigen, pa_resample_nfact, sample == "ar_nhb")`). Parallel
  analysis on tetrachoric correlations of items with a guessing floor is
  uninformative here: it neither supports June's 11 nor settles on a
  number. The bifactor models below are the better test.

## What the covariance follows: question type, story or construct

For each item pair, the tetrachoric correlation is compared within vs
between groupings (June's method). Intervals are ± 1.96 bootstrap SD over
200 person resamples. In a fixed form, story type ("old group") gives
exactly the same numbers as story, because each form has one story per
story type, so it is omitted. "Question type (different stories)" compares
only pairs from different stories, so it is not confounded with story.

Tetrachoric correlations are not a clean test of grouping here. Question
type explains about a third of item difficulty, and items of similar
difficulty with the same guessing floor correlate more on the tetrachoric
scale even under one factor. The same contrasts are therefore also computed
on Q3, the residual correlations after the unidimensional 2PL + guessing
model of the local-dependence section, which models difficulty and
guessing. Their intervals come from a person bootstrap of the residual
matrix (item parameters and θ held fixed).

```{r grouping}
res_dim$grouping_contrast |>
  filter(sample %in% c(dim_primary, "ar_nhb_nofb", "de_ib_junelike"), grouping != "old group") |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], grouping, n_within, n_between, mean_within, mean_between,
            within_minus_between, diff_lo, diff_hi) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Within- minus between-group mean tetrachoric r")
res_dim$q3_grouping_contrast |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary, grouping != "old group") |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], grouping, n_within, n_between, mean_within, mean_between,
            within_minus_between, diff_lo, diff_hi) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "The same contrasts on Q3 residual correlations (2PL + guessing, unidimensional)")
```

```{r fig-cells, fig.height=5.5}
res_dim$grouping_cells |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  mutate(sample = factor(dim_labels[sample], dim_labels[dim_primary]),
         panel = if_else(str_detect(cell, "construct"), "Construct", "Story × type"),
         cell = fct_inorder(cell)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_r, y = fct_rev(cell), colour = sample)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = r_lo, xmax = r_hi), position = position_dodge(width = .6)) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(panel), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = set_names(dim_pal, dim_labels[names(dim_pal)]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Mean tetrachoric r (± 1.96 bootstrap SD)", y = NULL,
       title = "The 'story effect' lives in same-story, same-type pairs") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r dim-numbers}
gc <- res_dim$grouping_contrast
qt_contrast <- gc$within_minus_between[gc$grouping == "question type" & gc$sample %in% dim_primary]
st_contrast <- gc$within_minus_between[gc$grouping == "story" & gc$sample %in% dim_primary]
nc_contrast <- gc$within_minus_between[gc$grouping == "new construct" & gc$sample %in% dim_primary]
gcell <- res_dim$grouping_cells
q3c <- res_dim$q3_grouping_contrast |> filter(sample %in% dim_primary)
q3_qt <- q3c |> filter(grouping == "question type")
q3_st <- q3c |> filter(grouping == "story")
q3_qt_ds <- q3c |> filter(grouping == "question type (different stories)")
k$q3_qt_le_story <- sum(q3_qt$within_minus_between <= q3_st$within_minus_between[match(q3_qt$sample, q3_st$sample)])
qt_ds <- gc$within_minus_between[gc$grouping == "question type (different stories)" & gc$sample %in% dim_primary]
```

- **Question type** has a reliably positive tetrachoric contrast in every
  sample (`r rng(qt_contrast, 3)`, all pairs; `r rng(qt_ds, 3)` among
  different-story pairs), smaller than June's .101. The June-style rebuild of the Leipzig
  data gives
  `r n2(pick(gc, within_minus_between, sample == "de_ib_junelike", grouping == "question type"), 3)`.
  That rebuild differs from the primary sample in item identities,
  exclusions, runs (all vs first per child) and items all at once, so the
  change cannot be assigned to any one of them. On Q3 residuals the
  question-type contrast shrinks to `r rng(q3_qt$within_minus_between, 3)`
  (`r rng(q3_qt_ds$within_minus_between, 3)` among different-story pairs)
  and is no larger than the story contrast in `r k$q3_qt_le_story` of the
  `r nrow(q3_qt)` samples. It vanishes in Leipzig
  (`r n2(pick(q3_qt, within_minus_between, sample == "de_ib"), 3)`) and
  stays clearly positive in Western
  (`r n2(pick(q3_qt, within_minus_between, sample == "wca_ib"), 3)`). Part of
  the tetrachoric clustering by question type therefore reflects shared
  difficulty and guessing; what remains once they are modelled is weak and
  differs between samples.
- **Story** contrasts are `r rng(st_contrast, 3)` (Q3:
  `r rng(q3_st$within_minus_between, 3)`), and they come entirely
  from pairs of the same story *and* the same question type. In Leipzig,
  same-story pairs of the same type correlate
  `r n2(pick(gcell, mean_r, sample == "de_ib", cell == "same story, same question type"), 3)`;
  same-story pairs of different types correlate
  `r n2(pick(gcell, mean_r, sample == "de_ib", cell == "same story, different question type"), 3)`,
  no more than pairs from different stories.
- **Constructs** organize little (`r rng(nc_contrast, 3)`). The only test
  not confounded with story compares different-story pairs in the same
  construct with pairs across constructs. In the three stories 1–6 forms,
  same-construct pairs correlate less (Leipzig
  `r n2(pick(gcell, mean_r, sample == "de_ib", cell == "different story, same new construct"), 3)`
  vs `r n2(pick(gcell, mean_r, sample == "de_ib", cell == "different story, different new construct"), 3)`).
  es-AR is the exception: its construct contrast is reliably positive
  (`r n2(pick(gc, within_minus_between, sample == "ar_nhb", grouping == "new construct"), 3)`
  [`r n2(pick(gc, diff_lo, sample == "ar_nhb", grouping == "new construct"), 3)`,
  `r n2(pick(gc, diff_hi, sample == "ar_nhb", grouping == "new construct"), 3)`]),
  and it roughly halves without the flagged story-13 item
  (`r n2(pick(gc, within_minus_between, sample == "ar_nhb_nofb", grouping == "new construct"), 3)`).
  June's table showed .045 for constructs, above story's .039, although its
  prose called the construct contrast "near zero". On Leipzig data, that
  contrast reproduces only on the uncorrected, June-style rebuild
  (`r n2(pick(gc, within_minus_between, sample == "de_ib_junelike", grouping == "new construct"), 3)`).
- Cleaning raised the mean inter-item correlation from
  `r n2(pick(res_dim$eigen, mean_offdiag_r, sample == "de_ib_junelike"), 3)`
  (June-style rebuild) to
  `r rng(res_dim$eigen$mean_offdiag_r[res_dim$eigen$sample %in% dim_primary], 3)`.
  The defective items had depressed the between-group baseline.

```{r efa}
res_dim$efa2_summary |>
  filter(sample %in% c(dim_primary, "ar_nhb_nofb", "de_ib_junelike")) |>
  mutate(sample = dim_labels[sample]) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Two-factor oblimin EFA of the tetrachoric matrix")
res_dim$efa2_by_qtype |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  mutate(sample = dim_labels[sample]) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = c(n, F1, F2), names_vary = "slowest") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mean loadings on F1/F2 by question type")
```

A two-factor EFA still gives no sub-construct that replicates. What defines
the second factor changes from sample to sample: nothing in Leipzig, an
emotion factor in Western, and a split between controls and targets in
es-AR.

## Local dependence

A 2PL with guessing fixed at chance was fitted as a unidimensional model
and as bifactor models with story testlets or question-type factors. Items
answered at or below chance in the sample get a floor of 0, because a fixed
floor above the observed rate cannot fit; the reliability and invariance
models keep the floor at chance and are rerun under this rule as a check. Every slope has an N(0, 2²) prior (MAP-EM); without
it, fixed-floor fits diverge. AIC and BIC are evaluated at the MAP
estimates. dAIC and dBIC are bifactor minus unidimensional, so negative
values favour the bifactor.

```{r ld}
res_dim$irt_ld |>
  filter(family == "guess", sample %in% c(dim_primary, "ar_nhb_nofb")) |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], n_items, n_persons, dAIC_story, dBIC_story,
            dAIC_qtype, dBIC_qtype, ECV, omega_h, omega_total, omega_h_over_t = omega_h / omega_total,
            PUC, rxx_uni,
            cor_theta_uni_general, info_overstatement, q3_within_story, q3_between_story,
            `within-story pairs with Q3 > .2` = paste0(`n_within_q3_gt_.2`, "/", n_within_pairs)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Unidimensional vs bifactor 2PL + guessing")
```

- There is some story-level dependence, but little of consequence. The
  story bifactor improves AIC in every sample. BIC prefers the
  unidimensional model in the three smaller samples and is indifferent in
  es-AR. θ from the two models correlates `r k$cor_uni_g`.
- **How dominant is the general factor?** ECV is `r k$ecv`, below the
  usual .70 guideline in Leipzig
  (`r n2(pick(ld, ECV, sample == "de_ib"))`) and es-AR
  (`r n2(pick(ld, ECV, sample == "ar_nhb"))`). Omega-h (`r k$omh`) comes
  from standardized normal-ogive loadings that ignore the guessing floor, so
  it is not comparable with the observed-score reliabilities elsewhere in
  this chapter. It is also inflated by story factors whose specific
  loadings mix signs (`r k$mixed_stories` of `r k$n_story_factors` story
  factors in the four samples; in Leipzig story 2, Σ|λs| =
  `r n2(k$de_s2_abs)` but |Σλs| = `r n2(k$de_s2_sum)`), and 2-item testlets
  are identified only through the slope prior. The ratio omega-h / omega-t
  (`r rng(ld$omega_h / ld$omega_total)`) is the safer summary. By that
  ratio the general factor dominates in every sample; by ECV it dominates
  clearly only in Western and Bogotá, and in Leipzig and es-AR the case for
  it is weaker.
- The unidimensional model overstates test information by `r k$info_over`,
  in line with the September audit's roughly
  `r pct(pick(res_dim$june_reference, june_value, metric == "information overstatement (uni vs bifactor)"))`
  on the v2_3 calibration data.
- A question-type bifactor fits as well as the story bifactor, and in es-AR
  clearly better. Most of the es-AR advantage comes from the below-chance
  Spanish false-belief item: without story 13's item, dBIC for the
  question-type model goes from
  `r n2(pick(res_dim$irt_ld, dBIC_qtype, family == "guess", sample == "ar_nhb"), 0)` to
  `r n2(pick(res_dim$irt_ld, dBIC_qtype, family == "guess", sample == "ar_nhb_nofb"), 0)`.

The residual dependence sits in a handful of "doublets". Most are yes/no
questions about the same scene with the same key. One pair of location
false-belief questions from different stories behaves the same way:

```{r doublets}
res_dim$ld_pairs_top |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], item_i = uid_label(i), item_j = uid_label(j),
            same_story, r, q3, code_i, answer_i, p_i, code_j, answer_j, p_j) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Item pairs with Q3 > .2 (2PL + guessing, unidimensional)")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Robustness: the same models without a guessing floor

```{r ld-noguess}
res_dim$irt_ld |>
  filter(family == "noguess") |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], dAIC_story, dBIC_story, dAIC_qtype, dBIC_qtype,
            ECV, omega_h, cor_theta_uni_general, info_overstatement) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
:::

## Sub-scales

```{r subscales}
res_dim$subscales |>
  filter(sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  transmute(sample = dim_labels[sample], scale, n_items, alpha, alpha_sb_to_all,
            twopl_marginal_rxx, rasch_marginal_rxx, age_r, age_r_lo, age_r_hi,
            pct_rand_alpha_below, pct_rand_age_r_below) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Sub-scales. alpha_sb_to_all projects alpha to the full scale's length (Spearman–Brown). pct_rand_* is the percentile among 500 random item subsets of the same size.")
```

```{r fig-subscales, fig.height=4.5}
ss <- res_dim$subscales |> filter(sample %in% dim_primary) |>
  mutate(sample = factor(dim_labels[sample], dim_labels[dim_primary]),
         scale = factor(scale, c("all items", "targets only", "false-belief only", "controls only")))
ggplot(ss, aes(x = scale, y = age_r)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = rand_age_r_q025, ymax = rand_age_r_q975), linewidth = 4,
                 colour = "grey80", data = filter(ss, scale != "all items")) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = age_r_lo, ymax = age_r_hi)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(sample), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = levels(ss$scale)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "r(proportion correct, age)",
       title = "Age validity of sub-scales against random item subsets of the same size (grey)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

June's answer stands: no sub-scale improves on the full set. False-belief
items are the most internally consistent per item (Spearman–Brown-projected
alpha `r rng(res_dim$subscales$alpha_sb_to_all[res_dim$subscales$scale == "false-belief only" & res_dim$subscales$sample %in% dim_primary])`),
but a false-belief-only scale is no more age-valid than random subsets. In
es-AR it is less age-valid than the full scale. The controls are the least
age-valid items (discussed next).

# Controls

This section re-tests June's claims about the reality-check (control)
questions: that they correlate with targets, that they do not gate the
targets' age sensitivity, and that keeping them helps reliability.

```{r controls-cor}
res_items$controls_cor |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Person-level correlations of control and target accuracy (runs with age)")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Within each dataset × form

```{r controls-cells}
res_items$controls_cells |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  select(-cell) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
:::

Pooled over runs, as June did it, control and target accuracy correlate
`r n2(k$r_ct_pooled)`. Much of that is between-site differences: within
dataset × form the correlation is `r n2(k$r_ct_within)`, and controls
correlate
`r n2(pick(cc, r_control_age, method == "within dataset x form, Fisher-pooled", item_set == "policy items dropped"))`
with age. These are accuracy scores, and fCAT runs have a median of
`r median(res_items$controls_cells$median_ctrl[res_items$controls_cells$form == "fcat_random3"])`
controls each, which attenuates the correlations.

## Gating

```{r gating}
res_items$gating_june |> select(-method) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "June method: lm(story target accuracy ~ scale(age)) by whether the story's control was passed")
res_items$gating_glmm |>
  mutate(interaction_p = fp(interaction_p)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "GLMM on target trials: correct ~ age × ctrl_pass + dataset + (1 | run) + (1 | story_uid). Slopes in logits per year.")
```

```{r fig-gating, fig.height=4.5}
res_items$gating_plot |>
  mutate(language = factor(language, lang_levels),
         ctrl_pass = if_else(ctrl_pass, "control passed", "control failed")) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_bin, target_acc, colour = ctrl_pass)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(size = n), alpha = .7) +
  facet_wrap(vars(language), nrow = 1) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("control passed" = "grey30", "control failed" = "#CC6677"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Target accuracy in the story",
       title = "Target accuracy by age, split by whether the story's control was passed") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r gating-numbers}
gg <- res_items$gating_glmm
g_all <- filter(gg, sample == "all languages"); g_de <- filter(gg, sample == "de-DE")
g_co  <- filter(gg, sample == "es-CO")
gj <- res_items$gating_june
```

June's method again finds no gating: the target age slope is
`r n2(pick(gj, target_age_beta_perSD, !ctrl_pass), 3)` per SD of age after
a failed control and `r n2(pick(gj, target_age_beta_perSD, ctrl_pass), 3)`
after a passed one. The trial-level GLMM finds a small pooled interaction
(`r n2(g_all$interaction, 3)` logits/yr, p = `r n2(g_all$interaction_p, 3)`).
It comes from de-DE, where targets after a failed control show no age slope
(`r n2(g_de$age_slope_fail, 3)` vs `r n2(g_de$age_slope_pass, 3)`;
`r n2(g_de$pct_instances_fail, 1)`% of story instances failed), and to a
lesser degree from en-US (`r n2(pick(gg, interaction, sample == "en-US"), 3)`,
p = `r n2(pick(gg, interaction_p, sample == "en-US"), 3)`); en-GB and es-AR
are borderline (p = `r n2(pick(gg, interaction_p, sample == "en-GB"), 3)` and
`r n2(pick(gg, interaction_p, sample == "es-AR"), 3)`). es-CO shows none
(`r n2(g_co$pct_instances_fail, 1)`% failed). Passing a control is itself related to ability, so this is a
description, not a causal gate. In a high-scoring sample like Leipzig, a
failed control probably marks a lapse.

## Do controls help the score?

On fixed forms, with guessing fixed at chance and production priors:

```{r controls-rel}
res_items$reliability |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  filter(row %in% c(1:8, 13:14)) |>
  select(sample, items, model, guessing, n_runs, n_items, n_controls, mean_items_answered,
         marginal_rxx_mirt, marginal_rxx, empirical_rxx, alpha_complete_cases,
         r_theta_age, r_theta_all_vs_targets) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Reliability and age validity with and without controls. The last two rows replicate June's method: pure Rasch without priors on June's 58-item Leipzig pool (item bank and retest forms, released identities, policy items kept).")
```

```{r controls-numbers}
rrow <- \(s, it, m, col) pick(res_items$reliability, {{ col }}, sample == s, items == it, model == m)
de_s <- "DE Leipzig, item-bank form (stories 1-6)"
ar_s <- "UTDT-AR main, no-HA retest-B form (stories 13-18)"
jn_s <- "DE Leipzig, June item pool (June method)"
# the items script and the dimensionality script replicate June's .92 on the same pool
stopifnot(abs(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", marginal_rxx_mirt) - jp$rasch_marginal_rxx_june_method) < .001,
          abs(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", empirical_rxx) - jp$rasch_empirical_rxx_eap) < .001)
k$dage_max <- res_items$reliability |> slice(1:8) |>
  select(sample, model, items, r_theta_age) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = items, values_from = r_theta_age) |>
  summarise(d = max(abs(`all items` - `targets only`))) |> pull(d)
```

- **Keep the controls.** They raise reliability a little: Leipzig
  `r n2(rrow(de_s, "all items", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` with them vs
  `r n2(rrow(de_s, "targets only", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` without; UTDT
  `r n2(rrow(ar_s, "all items", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` vs
  `r n2(rrow(ar_s, "targets only", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` (Rasch +
  guessing, empirical). They change r(θ, age) by at most
  `r n2(k$dage_max)`. June reached
  the same conclusion.
- **Per item, controls are the weakest.** The dimensionality analysis finds
  them the least age-valid items. In Leipzig a controls-only score
  correlates
  `r n2(pick(res_dim$subscales, age_r, sample == "de_ib", scale == "controls only"), 3)`
  with age, below
  `r pct(1 - pick(res_dim$subscales, pct_rand_age_r_below, sample == "de_ib", scale == "controls only"))`
  of random `r pick(res_dim$subscales, n_items, sample == "de_ib", scale == "controls only")`-item
  subsets. Once alpha is projected to equal length, targets
  alone match all items in every sample. Controls help the score as extra
  items, not as especially good ones.
- **June's .92 → .89.** That comparison reproduces as mirt's
  `marginal_rxx` on June's sparse
  `r rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", n_items)`-item Leipzig pool
  (`r n2(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", marginal_rxx_mirt), 3)` with
  controls vs `r n2(rrow(jn_s, "targets only", "Rasch", marginal_rxx_mirt), 3)`
  without; June: .915 vs .885). Children answered
  `r n2(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", mean_items_answered), 1)` of those
  items on average. The same fit's empirical reliability is
  `r n2(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` with controls
  and `r n2(rrow(jn_s, "targets only", "Rasch", empirical_rxx), 3)` without.
  `mirt::marginal_rxx()` integrates TI/(TI + var) over N(0, 1) and assumes
  every item is answered. With a Rasch latent variance of
  `r n2(rrow(jn_s, "all items", "Rasch", latent_var), 2)`, that inflates the
  value. The reliability section returns to this.

# Cross-language invariance

**Methods.** Multigroup Rasch with the guessing floor fixed at chance (the
LEVANTE convention), fitted with mirt. Each child contributes one run: the
earliest that contains the analysed stories. An item needs ≥ 100 responses
per group. The sequence is configural vs scalar, then a DIF screen with all
other items as anchors, then purified and iterated anchors, then partial
scalar. fCAT runs are included; their missing items are missing by design.
Effect sizes `db` are item difficulty for a group minus de-DE, in logits;
positive means harder at matched ability. dBIC = BIC(constrained) −
BIC(less constrained), so positive values favour the less constrained
model.

The ETS classes are adapted, not the ETS rule itself: A (negligible), B
(moderate) and C (large) use the 1- and 1.5-delta cut-offs (0.43 and 0.64
logits) on latent-logit db under the guessing floor, which runs larger than
the observed-score Mantel–Haenszel D-DIF they were defined for.
Significance is the item's BH-adjusted LR test, and class C does not
require |db| to be significantly above 0.43.

A maximum-likelihood 2PL was not usable: its configural models do not
converge, and slopes reach `r n2(max(res_inv$model_choice$max_slope), 0)`.
A 2PL with the production priors (d ~ N(0, 3), a ~ N(1, 0.3), MAP) is
usable and serves as the second model throughout: for the metric and
scalar tests, and for DIF effect sizes.

```{r model-choice}
res_inv$model_choice |>
  select(analysis, model, logLik, npar, BIC, converged, iterations, max_slope,
         prop_slopes_over_4, prop_slopes_negative) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Maximum-likelihood 2PL + guessing fits are degenerate")
```

```{r inv-samples}
res_inv$samples |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  select(analysis, group, n_children, age_median, age_q1, age_q3, age_missing, datasets, forms) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Analysis A: stories 1–6, de-DE vs en-US vs es-CO. Analysis B: stories 13–18, de-DE vs es-AR.")
```

```{r inv-exposure}
sB <- res_inv$samples |> filter(analysis == "B")
# how many earlier included ToM runs each analysed child had (the analysed run is the child's
# earliest run containing the analysed stories)
inc_runs <- runs |> filter(included) |> arrange(user_id, time_started) |>
  group_by(user_id) |> mutate(k_run = row_number()) |> ungroup()
first_with <- \(st, langs) trials |>
  filter(story %in% st, language %in% langs, !policy_exclude) |>
  distinct(user_id, run_id, time_started, language) |>
  arrange(time_started, run_id) |> group_by(user_id) |> slice(1) |> ungroup() |>
  left_join(inc_runs |> select(run_id, k_run), by = "run_id")
expB <- first_with(13:18, c("de-DE", "es-AR")) |>
  left_join(runs |> select(run_id, age), by = "run_id")
k$B_de_n <- sum(expB$language == "de-DE")
k$B_de_repeat <- sum(expB$language == "de-DE" & expB$k_run > 1)
k$B_ar_repeat <- sum(expB$language == "es-AR" & expB$k_run > 1)
k$Byoung_n <- sum(expB$language == "de-DE" & !is.na(expB$age) & expB$age < 9)
k$Byoung_repeat <- sum(expB$language == "de-DE" & !is.na(expB$age) & expB$age < 9 & expB$k_run > 1)
stopifnot(k$B_de_n == pick(sB, n_children, group == "de_DE"),
          k$Byoung_n == pick(res_inv$samples, n_children, analysis == "B_young", group == "de_DE"))
```

The groups are not language groups only. In stories 13–18 (analysis B),
`r k$B_de_repeat` of the `r k$B_de_n` German children
(`r pct(k$B_de_repeat / k$B_de_n)`) were on their second or third ToM run,
having taken stories 1–6 or 7–12 earlier;
`r if (k$B_ar_repeat == 0) "none of the es-AR children" else paste(k$B_ar_repeat, "es-AR children")`
were. The German children are older (median
`r n2(pick(sB, age_median, group == "de_DE"), 1)` vs
`r n2(pick(sB, age_median, group == "es_AR"), 1)` years), and es-AR comes
from one site (UTDT). In A, the German children are older too, and es-CO
pools four datasets from 2024–2026, including the V0 content. Group
differences in item difficulty are therefore differences between samples
that differ in language, age, prior exposure and site, and the estimated
group means (numerics note) are not language differences in theory of mind.

```{r inv-tests}
res_inv$tests |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  transmute(analysis, comparison, items, n_items, X2, df, X2_df, p = fp(p), dBIC) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Invariance tests, Rasch + guessing")
res_inv$tests_2pl |>
  transmute(analysis, comparison, df, X2_logLik, X2_logpost, p_logpost = fp(p_logpost), dBIC,
            nested_optimum_better) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Invariance tests, 2PL + guessing with production priors (MAP). X2 on the log-likelihood and on the log posterior; dBIC from mirt's BIC. A more constrained model reaching a better optimum (nested_optimum_better) means the less constrained fit found a local optimum, so only metric vs scalar is interpreted.")
```

```{r inv-test-numbers}
t2 <- \(a, cmp, col) pick(res_inv$tests_2pl, {{ col }}, analysis == a, comparison == cmp)
tr_ <- \(a, cmp, col, it = "all") pick(tst, {{ col }}, analysis == a, comparison == cmp, items == it)
isl <- res_rel$item_slopes_by_type
dlab <- res_inv$dif_long |> filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B"))
k$mdd_med <- median(dlab$mdd, na.rm = TRUE)
k$se_med  <- median(dlab$se, na.rm = TRUE)
k$mdd_B   <- median(dlab$mdd[dlab$analysis == "B"], na.rm = TRUE)
```

- **Stories 1–6 (A).** The LR test rejects scalar invariance under Rasch +
  guessing (χ²/df `r n2(k$A_scal_x2df, 1)`), but BIC is indifferent (dBIC
  `r n2(tr_("A", "scalar vs configural", dBIC), 1)`). Under the 2PL, BIC
  prefers the scalar model to the metric one (dBIC
  `r n2(t2("A", "scalar vs metric", dBIC), 0)`; LR on the log posterior
  p = `r n2(t2("A", "scalar vs metric", p_logpost), 2)`). Intercept
  differences are detectable, but neither model's BIC favours
  non-invariance. Without the V0 Bogotá runs, Rasch BIC prefers scalar too
  (dBIC `r n2(tr_("A_noV0", "scalar vs configural", dBIC), 0)`). The
  verdict depends on the guessing convention, though: with the floor set to
  0 for the two items answered at or below chance in a group, Rasch BIC
  rejects scalar invariance (dBIC `r n2(tr_("A_g0", "scalar vs configural", dBIC), 0)`).
  The evidence for non-invariance in stories 1–6 is model-dependent.
- **Stories 13–18 (B)** are non-invariant under both models (Rasch χ²/df
  `r n2(k$B_scal_x2df, 1)`, dBIC `r n2(tr_("B", "scalar vs configural", dBIC), 0)`;
  2PL dBIC `r n2(t2("B", "scalar vs metric", dBIC), 0)`, log-posterior LR
  p `r pe(t2("B", "scalar vs metric", p_logpost))`).
- Rasch DIF can partly be unequal slopes. The Rasch model forces equal
  discrimination, but false-belief items discriminate most (2PL median slope
  `r n2(pick(isl, median_a, question_type == "false_belief"))` vs
  `r n2(pick(isl, median_a, question_type == "reality_check"))` for
  controls), and the groups differ in mean ability.
- **Partial scalar invariance is a description, not a test.** The partial
  scalar models fit (p = `r n2(k$A_part_p)` in A, `r n2(k$B_part_p)` in B),
  but their anchors were chosen by the DIF screen on the same data, so the
  fit is expected. Without V0 Bogotá the partial scalar model is rejected
  (p = `r n2(tr_("A_noV0", "partial scalar vs configural", p), 4)`). Anchor status
  also reflects power: the median SE of db is `r n2(k$se_med)` logits, so
  an item's DIF would have to be about `r n2(k$mdd_med, 1)` logits to be
  detected with 80% power even before the BH adjustment
  (`r n2(k$mdd_B, 1)` in B, where the German group has
  `r k$B_de_n` children). "Class A" means "not detected".

```{r inv-dif}
rasch_db <- res_inv$dif |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A_rasch", "B_rasch")) |>
  transmute(analysis = str_remove(analysis, "_rasch"), short,
            rasch_db_en_US = db_en_US, rasch_db_es_CO = db_es_CO, rasch_db_es_AR = db_es_AR)
res_inv$dif |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B"), class != "A") |>
  left_join(rasch_db, by = c("analysis", "short")) |>
  mutate(across(c(db_en_US, db_es_CO, db_es_AR),
                \(x) if_else(boundary & abs(x) > 10, NA_real_, x))) |>
  transmute(analysis, item = uid_label(short), question_type,
            db_en_US, db_es_CO, db_es_AR, rasch_db_en_US, rasch_db_es_CO, rasch_db_es_AR,
            acc_de_DE, acc_en_US, acc_es_CO, acc_es_AR, class,
            note = case_when(boundary ~ "unbounded (below floor); read the Rasch db",
                             near_floor ~ "near floor; Rasch db smaller",
                             TRUE ~ "")) |>
  arrange(analysis, question_type) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Non-invariant items (class B or C). db = difficulty vs de-DE (logits, Rasch + guessing); rasch_db = the same from pure Rasch.")
```

```{r fig-dif, fig.height=9}
dl <- res_inv$dif_long |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  mutate(capped = abs(db) > 5,
         db_plot = pmax(pmin(db, 5), -5),
         item = fct_reorder(uid_label(short), -story),
         question_type = factor(question_type, qtype_levels),
         class = factor(class, c("A", "B", "C")),
         contrast = str_replace_all(contrast, "_", "-"))
ggplot(dl, aes(x = db_plot, y = item, colour = question_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = pmax(db - 1.96 * se, -5), xmax = pmin(db + 1.96 * se, 5)),
                 data = filter(dl, !is.na(se), !capped)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = class), size = 2.3) +
  geom_point(data = filter(dl, capped), shape = 62, size = 5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(contrast), nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(dl$item)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = qtype_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(A = 1, B = 17, C = 16), name = "ETS class") +
  labs(x = "db: difficulty vs de-DE (logits; capped at ±5, > = unbounded)", y = NULL,
       title = "Item DIF against de-DE",
       subtitle = "± 1.96 SE; anchors' db and SE come from freeing each anchor in turn") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r inv-numbers}
dq <- res_inv$dif_by_qtype
fb_A <- filter(dq, analysis == "A", question_type == "false_belief")
fb_B <- filter(dq, analysis == "B", question_type == "false_belief")
anc <- res_inv$dif |> filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  group_by(analysis) |> summarise(ctrl_anchor = sum(anchor & is_control),
                                  ctrl = sum(is_control), anchors = sum(anchor))
aba <- res_inv$age_band_acc
s3rc1 <- aba |> filter(short == "story3_interpretation_reality_check_1", n >= 20)
ctrl_flag <- \(a) pick(dbt, n_flagged, analysis == a, kind == "control")
ctrl_large_A <- res_inv$dif |> filter(analysis == "A", is_control, class == "C") |> pull(short)
noV0_class <- \(it) pick(res_inv$dif, class, analysis == "A_noV0", short == it)
dm <- res_inv$dif_by_type_models
dmv <- \(a, kd, col) pick(dm, {{ col }}, analysis == a, kind == kd)
ra <- res_inv$rasch_2pl_agreement
```

## Controls vs targets

June found controls to be the dominant source of cross-language
non-invariance (mean |DIF| ≈ 1.9 for controls vs ≈ 0.5 for targets). The
table below gives that metric (mean over items of the largest pairwise
difficulty gap, boundary items excluded) under both models, next to the
share of the DIF χ².

```{r inv-bytype-models}
dm |>
  transmute(analysis, kind, n_items, rasch_stage1 = rasch_s1, rasch_purified = rasch_s2,
            twopl_stage1 = twopl_s1, twopl_purified, n_large_2pl_purified) |>
  left_join(dbt |> filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
              select(analysis, kind, n_flagged, share_of_items, share_of_s1_X2),
            by = c("analysis", "kind")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mean |db| (logits) for controls and targets: Rasch + guessing (stage 1: all other items as anchors; purified: final anchors) and 2PL with priors (stage 1: all other non-boundary items as anchors; purified: the Rasch anchors minus boundary items). Boundary items excluded.")
ra |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Agreement of 2PL (stage 1) and Rasch (stage 1) db, by item type, with and without the boundary items")
```

- **Whether controls or targets carry more of the non-invariance depends
  on the model and the design.** In stories 1–6, controls are
  `r pct(k$A_ctrl_it)` of the items but carry `r pct(k$A_ctrl_x2)` of the
  stage-1 DIF χ², and their mean |db| is larger than the targets' under
  both models (Rasch `r n2(dmv("A", "control", rasch_s2))` vs
  `r n2(dmv("A", "target", rasch_s2))`; 2PL
  `r n2(dmv("A", "control", twopl_purified))` vs
  `r n2(dmv("A", "target", twopl_purified))`). Without V0 Bogotá it
  reverses (controls
  `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "A_noV0", kind == "control"))` vs
  targets `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "A_noV0", kind == "target"))`,
  Rasch). In stories 13–18 controls carry `r pct(k$B_ctrl_x2)` of the χ²
  and have the smaller Rasch |db|
  (`r n2(dmv("B", "control", rasch_s2))` vs `r n2(dmv("B", "target", rasch_s2))`),
  but the larger 2PL |db| (`r n2(dmv("B", "control", twopl_purified))` vs
  `r n2(dmv("B", "target", twopl_purified))`); for controls in B, the two
  models' db correlate only
  `r n2(pick(ra, r_controls_no_boundary, analysis == "B"))`. In June's own
  design on corrected data (J_policy, below), controls still exceed targets.
  The corrections shrank the controls' DIF, but "controls no longer drive
  the non-invariance" does not hold in general.
- **False-belief targets are non-invariant too.** `r fb_A$n_flagged` of
  `r fb_A$n_items` false-belief items are flagged in A and
  `r fb_B$n_flagged` of `r fb_B$n_items` in B. Most are harder in Spanish
  (story 4 fb_2 goes the other way), and the gaps persist at matched age
  (figure below). The flagged set is wider than the reality_known item:
  moral-reasoning, interpretation and second-order false-belief items are
  also non-invariant. (Story 14 fb_2 and fb_3 are yes/no moral judgments,
  such as "Is Bobby being mean and naughty…?", that the corpus classifies as
  false-belief questions.) Dropping the reality_known item alone changes
  almost nothing (flag agreement
  `r pct(min(res_inv$flag_agreement$agreement[res_inv$flag_agreement$analysis %in% c("A_nofb", "B_nofb")]))`).
- `r length(ctrl_large_A)` controls are large in A:
  `r paste(uid_label(ctrl_large_A), collapse = ", ")`. Story-2 reality
  check 2 and story 5's reference reality check are V0 Bogotá effects: both
  fall to class `r noV0_class("story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_2")`
  without V0 (next paragraph). **Story-3 reality check 1** ("fountain")
  stays class `r noV0_class("story3_interpretation_reality_check_1")`: it is
  harder for es-CO children at every age (accuracy by age band
  `r rng(s3rc1$acc[s3rc1$language == "es-CO"])` vs
  `r rng(s3rc1$acc[s3rc1$language == "de-DE"])` in de-DE), a candidate for a
  translation or stimulus check.

```{r fig-ageband, fig.height=6.5}
age_items <- c("story1_reality_known_false_belief", "story13_reality_known_false_belief",
               "story2_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1", "story14_moral_reasoning_false_belief_1",
               "story3_interpretation_false_belief", "story15_interpretation_false_belief",
               "story18_second_order_false_belief_1", "story3_interpretation_reality_check_1",
               "story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_2")
aba |>
  filter(short %in% age_items, n >= 20) |>
  mutate(item = factor(uid_label(short), uid_label(age_items)),
         language = factor(language, lang_levels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_band, acc, colour = language, group = language)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = chance), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(item), ncol = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = lang_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age band (years)", y = "Accuracy", title = "Non-invariant items by age band (cells with n ≥ 20; dashed = chance)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**The V0 Bogotá paragraph.** Story-2 reality check 2 is non-invariant in A
(db for es-CO =
`r n2(pick(res_inv$dif, db_es_CO, analysis == "A", short == "story2_moral_reasoning_reality_check_2"))`).
The effect sits in the first Bogotá content (May–June 2024). Dropping those
runs (A_noV0, n ≥ 90) moves it and story 5's reference reality check to
class `r noV0_class("story5_reference_reality_check")` and cuts the flagged
controls from `r ctrl_flag("A")` to `r ctrl_flag("A_noV0")`. The scalar
χ²/df falls from `r n2(k$A_scal_x2df, 1)` to
`r n2(tr_("A_noV0", "scalar vs configural", X2_df), 1)`, and BIC then
prefers scalar (dBIC `r n2(tr_("A_noV0", "scalar vs configural", dBIC), 0)`),
although the LR test still rejects it
(p `r pe(tr_("A_noV0", "scalar vs configural", p))`). This makes V0
story-2 reality check 2 a candidate for a story- and epoch-scoped row in the
Airtable table, next to V0 reality check 1. It is not applied here.

## Within-language comparisons: is it language?

If the DIF above were about language (for example, translation), two sites
that share a language should show little of it. Two such comparisons are
possible with ≥ 60–100 responses per item: UTDT-AR main vs UTDT-intl
(es-AR, stories 13–18, the same no-HA retest-B form; UTDT-intl children are
younger) and Bogotá vs rural Colombia (es-CO, stories 1–6). A German
subsample matched more closely on age (under 9 years) repeats B.
First-exposure German children in B number only
`r k$B_de_n - k$B_de_repeat`, too few for DIF.

```{r inv-within}
wl <- c("X_esAR", "X_esCO", "B_young")
res_inv$samples |>
  filter(analysis %in% wl) |>
  select(analysis, group, n_children, age_median, age_q1, age_q3, datasets, forms) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Within-language and age-restricted samples")
res_inv$tests |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B", wl), items == "all", comparison == "scalar vs configural") |>
  transmute(analysis, n_items, X2, df, X2_df, p = fp(p), dBIC) |>
  left_join(res_inv$dif_by_type |> filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B", wl)) |>
              group_by(analysis) |>
              summarise(n_flagged = sum(n_flagged), n_large = sum(n_large),
                        mean_abs_db_controls = mean_abs_db[kind == "control"],
                        mean_abs_db_targets = mean_abs_db[kind == "target"], .groups = "drop"),
            by = "analysis") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Scalar vs configural and flagged items: between languages (A, B), within a language across sites (X_esAR, X_esCO), and B with German children under 9 (B_young)")
res_inv$dif |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("X_esAR", "X_esCO"), class != "A") |>
  transmute(analysis, item = uid_label(short), question_type, db_utdt_intl, db_rural, class,
            boundary) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Flagged items within a language (db = second site minus first)")
```

```{r within-numbers}
wl_t <- \(a, col) pick(tst, {{ col }}, analysis == a, comparison == "scalar vs configural", items == "all")
wl_f <- \(a) sum(res_inv$dif$class[res_inv$dif$analysis == a] != "A")
wl_n <- \(a) sum(res_inv$dif$analysis == a)
wl_qt <- \(a) res_inv$dif |> filter(analysis == a, class != "A") |> count(question_type) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |> mutate(x = paste(n, str_replace_all(question_type, "_", " "))) |>
  pull(x) |> paste(collapse = ", ")
fa <- res_inv$flag_agreement
```

- **Sites that share a language also differ, but less, and on other
  items.** Within es-AR, the two UTDT samples (same form; UTDT-intl
  children are younger) differ in `r wl_f("X_esAR")` of `r wl_n("X_esAR")`
  items, mostly emotion questions (`r wl_qt("X_esAR")`), and BIC prefers
  scalar invariance (dBIC `r n2(wl_t("X_esAR", dBIC), 0)`). Between de-DE
  and es-AR it is `r wl_f("B")` of `r wl_n("B")` items, mostly false belief
  (`r wl_qt("B")`), and BIC rejects scalar invariance (dBIC
  `r n2(wl_t("B", dBIC), 0)`). Within es-CO, Bogotá and rural Colombia
  differ in `r wl_f("X_esCO")` of `r wl_n("X_esCO")` items, including the two
  V0-driven controls (dBIC `r n2(wl_t("X_esCO", dBIC), 0)`).
- **Age does not explain the false-belief DIF in B.** With German children
  under 9 (median age
  `r n2(pick(res_inv$samples, age_median, analysis == "B_young", group == "de_DE"), 1)`
  vs `r n2(pick(res_inv$samples, age_median, analysis == "B_young", group == "es_AR"), 1)`
  in es-AR), B flags `r wl_f("B_young")` of `r wl_n("B_young")` items,
  largely the same false-belief items (flag agreement with B
  `r pct(pick(fa, agreement, analysis == "B_young"))`). Most of these
  younger German children were on a repeat run too
  (`r k$Byoung_repeat` of `r k$Byoung_n`), so prior exposure is not
  separated.
- The false-belief DIF between German and Argentine children is therefore
  not the generic difference between two sites, and it is not an age
  effect alone. Translation, prior exposure to the task and the samples
  themselves remain possible causes, and these data cannot separate them.

## The June bridge

```{r inv-bytype}
res_inv$dif_by_type |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("J_release", "J_policy", "A", "A_noV0", "A_policy", "B")) |>
  mutate(analysis = factor(analysis, c("J_release", "J_policy", "A", "A_noV0", "A_policy", "B"))) |>
  arrange(analysis, kind) |>
  select(analysis, kind, n_items, n_flagged, n_boundary, share_of_items, share_of_flagged,
         share_of_s1_X2, mean_abs_db) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Controls vs targets. J_*: June's design (DE-Leipzig vs Bogotá, pure Rasch, all runs, raw p < .05). J_release = release-equivalent data; J_policy = corrected + policy exclusions. A_policy puts the policy-excluded trials back.")
```

```{r june-bridge}
res_inv$june_bridge |>
  transmute(analysis, items, n_items, X2, df, X2_df, dBIC,
            X2_change_vs_release = pct(X2_change_vs_release),
            dBIC_change_vs_release = pct(dBIC_change_vs_release)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Scalar vs configural in June's design, on today's data")
res_inv$june_reported |>
  # the June chapters moved to old/ after this results file was built
  mutate(source = str_replace(source, "^tasks/tom_dif_multigroup", "old/tom_dif_multigroup")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "June's reported values (quoted from the June chapters, not recomputed)")
```

```{r bridge-numbers}
jb <- res_inv$june_bridge
jbv <- \(a, it, col) pick(jb, {{ col }}, analysis == a, items == it)
```

- **June's baseline reproduces on today's release-equivalent data:** χ²/df
  `r n2(jbv("J_release", "all", X2_df), 1)` (June ≈ 29), and mean |DIF|
  `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "J_release", kind == "control"))`
  for controls vs
  `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "J_release", kind == "target"))`
  for targets (June ≈ 1.9 vs 0.5). The released trials therefore still carry
  the June defects.
- **Corrections plus policy exclusions remove about half of the misfit in
  June's design:** χ² `r big(round(jbv("J_release", "all", X2)))` →
  `r big(round(jbv("J_policy", "all", X2)))`
  (`r spct(jbv("J_policy", "all", X2_change_vs_release))`), and
  `r pct(-jbv("J_policy", "controls", X2_change_vs_release))` of the
  controls' misfit. June reported about 70% overall. PR #27 alone does not
  reduce misfit (J_corrected
  `r spct(jbv("J_corrected", "all", X2_change_vs_release))`), because it
  restores data to the defective items. The reduction comes from the
  exclusions. June's repair also differed: it flipped keys and dropped the
  hostile-attribution epoch, whose `correct` values the audit found valid.
- In June's DE-vs-Bogotá design on corrected data (J_policy), controls
  still exceed targets (mean |DIF|
  `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "J_policy", kind == "control"))`
  vs `r n2(pick(dbt, mean_abs_db, analysis == "J_policy", kind == "target"))`),
  consistent with V0 Bogotá content driving part of it.

```{r flag-agreement}
res_inv$flag_agreement |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Agreement of flagged / not-flagged status with the primary analysis")
```

The flags hold across the fCAT, guessing-floor (pure Rasch; floor 0 for
items at or below chance, the dimensionality analysis's rule), Spanish
false-belief and policy choices (agreement
`r rng(fa$agreement[fa$analysis %in% c("A_policy", "A_nofb", "A_fixed", "A_rasch", "A_g0", "B_policy", "B_nofb", "B_rasch", "B_g0")])`).
The exceptions are A_noV0
(`r n2(pick(fa, agreement, analysis == "A_noV0"))`), because several

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Numerics, anchors, group parameters, and the 2PL cross-check

All `r big(sum(res_inv$convergence$n_fits))` Rasch-family fits converged.
`r sum(res_inv$convergence$n_fits_warned)` fits (in
`r paste(unique(res_inv$convergence$analysis[res_inv$convergence$n_fits_warned > 0]), collapse = ", ")`)
emitted mirt's "log-likelihood decreasing near the ML solution" warning.
Refitting with 121 instead of 61 quadrature points changes identified
difficulties by at most
`r n2(max(res_inv$numerics$max_abs_b_diff_identified), 3)` logits. The two
es-AR items below the guessing floor (story 13 FB, story 14 fb_1) are
unidentified in the Rasch + guessing model; their magnitudes come from
pure Rasch, and they are never 2PL anchors. With the floor set to 0 for
items at or below chance (A_g0, B_g0:
`r paste(uid_label(unique(unlist(res_inv$g0_items[c("A_g0", "B_g0")]))), collapse = ", ")`)
they are identified, and the flags barely change (agreement above). mirt's default θ range ([−6, 6]) was used throughout. The
reliability analysis shows that this range biases the means and variances
of low-scoring groups. The quadrature check varied the number of points,
not the range, so the effect on these fits is untested. It is likely small
for DIF, which the anchors identify, but the group means below should not be
used.

```{r inv-appendix}
res_inv$anchors |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  transmute(analysis, n_items, n_anchors, anchor_rule, anchors_stable,
            anchors = str_replace_all(anchors, "story", "S")) |>
  knitr::kable()
res_inv$group_pars |> filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
res_inv$numerics |> knitr::kable(digits = 4)
res_inv$robust_2pl |>
  transmute(analysis, item = uid_label(str_remove(item, "^tom_")), group, boundary, anchor_2pl, a,
            db_2pl, db_2pl_purified, db_rasch_stage1, db_rasch_stage2) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Item DIF under the 2PL with production priors and under Rasch + guessing")
```
:::

# Reliability, stability and age validity

## Scoring model

The analysis model is one 2PL, multigroup by dataset (each dataset with at
least `r res_rel$meta$min_group_runs` runs has its own mean and variance;
DE = N(0, 1)), scalar, with
guessing fixed at chance and production priors (d ~ N(0, 3),
a ~ N(1, 0.3)). It has `r res_rel$meta$n_items_analysis` items after the
policy exclusions and is calibrated concurrently. The θ range is [−12, 8]
with 201 quadrature points.

```{r itemtype}
res_rel$itemtype_bic |>
  select(model, itemtype, grid, runs, items, groups, n_par, logLik, AIC, BIC, converged) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Model comparison and variants (all converged)")
res_rel$item_slopes_by_type |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Item slopes by question type")
```

```{r fig-ab, fig.height=4.5}
res_rel$item_pars |>
  mutate(question_type = factor(question_type, qtype_levels),
         b_plot = pmax(pmin(b, 4), -8)) |>
  ggplot(aes(b_plot, a, colour = question_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = .8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = qtype_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Difficulty b (DE scale; clipped to [−8, 4])", y = "Slope a",
       title = "2PL item parameters: false-belief items discriminate most, emotion items least") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

BIC prefers the 2PL over the Rasch version
(dBIC `r n2(pick(res_rel$itemtype_bic, dBIC, model == "analysis", itemtype == "Rasch"), 0)`),
but scores barely depend on the choice (within-dataset r between the two
EAPs `r rng(res_rel$released_comparison$r_analysis_alt_itemtype[!res_rel$released_comparison$dataset %in% c(small_groups, "all (pooled)")], 3)`).
Story 17's emotion question has a slope of
`r n2(pick(res_rel$item_pars, a, str_starts(item, "tom_story17_reference_emotion_reasoning_1")), 3)`.
`r pct(pick(res_rel$item_pars, p_correct, str_starts(item, "tom_story17_reference_emotion_reasoning_1")))`
of children answer it correctly (chance .25), and it carries no
information about ability.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The low tail: group means and variances of low-scoring groups are weakly identified

mirt's default θ range is [−6, 6] with 61 points, and production uses it.
It cuts off the low tail of the lower-scoring groups and pulls their means
and variances toward the German reference. The analysis grid [−12, 8] is
numerically converged: a fit on [−16, 8] changes parameters and EAPs by at
most `r n2(max(res_rel$grid_convergence$max_abs_diff), 4)`. That shows the
integral is accurate, not that the tail is identified. Below θ ≈ −4 a child
who answers at or below guessing has an almost flat likelihood, so there the
normal prior, not the data, sets the lower tail. Two checks show how much
this matters:

- **Latent density.** With the items fixed at the analysis calibration,
  a nonparametric (empirical-histogram) density per group gives variances
  of `r n2(dc("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", var_eh), 1)` instead of
  `r n2(dc("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", var_normal), 1)` in UTDT-intl and
  `r n2(dc("pilot_uniandes_co_rural", var_eh), 1)` instead of
  `r n2(dc("pilot_uniandes_co_rural", var_normal), 1)` in rural Colombia,
  while EAPs under the two densities correlate
  `r rng(res_rel$density_check$r_eap_normal_eh)`.
- **Guessing rule.** With the floor set to 0 for the
  `r length(res_rel$meta$g0_items)` items answered at or below chance in some
  group (the dimensionality analysis's rule), the low-scoring groups'
  variances roughly halve (UTDT-intl
  `r n2(g0s("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", var_analysis), 1)` →
  `r n2(g0s("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", var_g0), 1)`, Bogotá
  `r n2(g0s("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota", var_analysis), 1)` →
  `r n2(g0s("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota", var_g0), 1)`), and their means rise
  by up to `r n2(max(res_rel$g0_sensitivity$mean_g0 - res_rel$g0_sensitivity$mean_analysis), 1)`.
  BIC prefers this version of the model by
  `r n2(pick(res_rel$itemtype_bic, BIC, model == "analysis", itemtype == "2PL") - pick(res_rel$itemtype_bic, BIC, str_starts(model, "analysis, floor 0")), 0)`,
  so the LEVANTE convention fits these items worse.

Rank order within a dataset barely moves in any of these checks (EAP
correlations `r rng(res_rel$g0_sensitivity$r_analysis_g0)` for the guessing
rule), and empirical reliability changes little. Group levels and
variances of low-scoring groups, however, depend on the grid, the density
and the guessing convention. This applies to the released v2_3 scores and
probably to other multigroup tasks with low-scoring groups; that is
untested. It is a DCC item to investigate before any production change.

```{r grid}
res_rel$grid_sensitivity |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), n_runs,
            mean_default = mean_defaultgrid, var_default = var_defaultgrid,
            mean_wide = mean_analysis, var_wide = var_analysis,
            r_wide_default, max_abs_shift, n_shift_gt_0.25, min_eap_default, min_eap_wide,
            rel_empirical_default, rel_empirical_wide) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Default vs wide integration grid")
res_rel$density_check |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), n_runs, mean_normal, var_normal, mean_eh, var_eh,
            post_mass_below_m4, r_eap_normal_eh, rel_empirical_normal, rel_empirical_eh,
            r_age_normal, r_age_eh, em_iterations, em_last_change) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Normal vs empirical-histogram group density (items fixed at the analysis calibration). post_mass_below_m4 = mean posterior mass below θ = −4 under the normal prior.")
res_rel$g0_sensitivity |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), n_runs, mean_analysis, mean_g0, var_analysis, var_g0,
            r_analysis_g0, rel_empirical_analysis, rel_empirical_g0, r_age_analysis, r_age_g0) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Guessing floor at chance (analysis) vs 0 for items at or below chance in a group (g0)")
```
:::

## Reliability per administration

Empirical reliability is var(EAP) / (var(EAP) + mean SE²) within a
dataset × form. `rel_group` instead uses the model's group variance in the
denominator (1 − mean SE² / σ²_g). All of these come from a
unidimensional model that assumes scalar invariance across datasets.[^upper]

[^upper]: Both assumptions make them upper bounds. The dimensionality
analysis finds that the unidimensional model overstates test information by
`r k$info_over`, which lowers reliability by
`r rng(ld$rxx_uni - ld$rxx_general, 3)` in its samples; and scalar
invariance does not fully hold (see the invariance section).

```{r rel-head}
rel_head |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), kind, n_runs, median_items, median_minutes,
            mean_prop_correct, prop_near_ceiling, prop_at_or_below_guessing,
            rms_se, rel_empirical, rel_group) |>
  arrange(kind, dataset) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Reliability per dataset, pooling each dataset's fixed forms, and of the fCAT (datasets with < 25 runs omitted)")
rel_forms |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), form, n_runs, median_items, mean_prop_correct,
            prop_near_ceiling, rel_empirical, rel_group) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Reliability of single fixed forms (dataset × form with ≥ 25 runs)")
res_rel$fcat_vs_fixed |>
  filter(form_type == "fixed form") |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), se_ratio_fcat_to_fixed, info_per_minute_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "fCAT vs fixed forms within a dataset: RMS SE ratio and information per minute ratio (different children)")
```

```{r fig-se, fig.height=6}
res_rel$scores_plot |>
  filter(!dataset %in% small_groups) |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset),
         form_type = if_else(str_starts(form_type, "fCAT"), "fCAT (3 random stories)", "fixed form")) |>
  ggplot(aes(eap, se, colour = form_type)) +
  geom_point(size = .6, alpha = .4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset), nrow = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-6, -3, 0)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("fixed form" = "grey30", "fCAT (3 random stories)" = "#CC6677"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "EAP θ (DE scale)", y = "Posterior SD",
       title = "Measurement precision by ability: the story bank is thin above θ = 0") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r rel-numbers}
de_fc <- filter(rel_head, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", kind != "fixed forms")
ffx <- res_rel$fcat_vs_fixed |> filter(form_type == "fixed form")
ffx_de <- pick(ffx, info_per_minute_ratio, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main")
ffx_other <- ffx$info_per_minute_ratio[ffx$dataset != "pilot_mpieva_de_main"]
```

- Pooling each dataset's fixed forms, a fixed form (median
  `r k$fixed_items` items) gives `r k$rel_fixed` per administration. Single
  forms range more widely, from `r n2(min(rel_forms$rel_empirical))`
  (`r k$low_form`) to `r n2(max(rel_forms$rel_empirical))`
  (`r k$high_form`). The deployed fCAT gives `r k$rel_fcat` in a median of
  `r k$fcat_min` minutes.
- Leipzig is the least reliably measured sample because it is near ceiling.
  `r pct(de_fc$prop_near_ceiling)` of its fCAT runs are ≥ 90% correct, and
  its fCAT reliability is `r n2(de_fc$rel_empirical)`.
- Per minute, the fCAT is at least as efficient as the fixed forms outside
  Leipzig (ratio `r rng(ffx_other)`); in Leipzig, where it is at ceiling,
  the ratio is `r n2(ffx_de)`. fCAT and fixed-form runs come from different
  children, who differ in age and ceiling rates, so these ratios are only
  indicative. The within-child simulation below is the cleaner comparison.

### Block CAT: a within-child simulation

The deployed fCAT shows one random story from each of three blocks, always
in the same order (block 1: stories `r paste(blk(1), collapse = ", ")`;
block 2: `r paste(blk(2), collapse = ", ")`; block 3:
`r paste(blk(3), collapse = ", ")`), so block and position are
confounded. To compare story selections in the same children,
every fixed-form run was rescored with the analysis model on (i) its whole
form, (ii) an fCAT-style random draw of one of its stories per block
(averaged over all draws), and (iii) an adaptive draw that takes, block by
block, the story whose items carry the most information at the child's
current EAP. Minutes are the child's own time on the chosen stories.
Reliability here is model-based (1 − mean posterior variance / σ²_g).

```{r cat-sim}
res_rel$cat_sim_summary |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), form, n_runs,
            min_full = median_minutes_full, min_random = median_minutes_random,
            min_adaptive = median_minutes_adaptive,
            rel_full, rel_random, rel_adaptive,
            info_per_min_full, info_per_min_random, info_per_min_adaptive,
            prop_adaptive_better) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fixed-form runs rescored on three stories: random (fCAT-style) vs adaptive selection within blocks, and the whole form")
```

- Three random stories take half the time of the whole form and cost
  `r rng(cs$rel_full - cs$rel_random)` in reliability.
- Choosing the more informative story in each block, in the same time,
  raises reliability by a median of
  `r n2(median(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random))` (range
  `r rng(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random)` across forms; UTDT-AR, the
  largest sample: `r n2(csv("rfp1_utdt_ar_main", rel_random))` →
  `r n2(csv("rfp1_utdt_ar_main", rel_adaptive))`, against
  `r n2(csv("rfp1_utdt_ar_main", rel_full))` for the whole form). It gives
  the lower posterior variance for
  `r pct(min(cs$prop_adaptive_better))`–`r pct(max(cs$prop_adaptive_better))`
  of children. The gain is smallest in the Leipzig retest-A form.
- The simulation can only choose between the stories a fixed form contains
  (two per block). The bank has six per block, so real adaptive selection
  could do more, provided the stories are calibrated in each language.

### Reconciling the reliability estimates

Three analyses estimate reliability for the same fixed forms, using
different person sets, item filters and priors:

```{r rel-reconcile}
irel <- \(s, m, col = empirical_rxx)
  pick(res_items$reliability, {{ col }}, sample == s, items == "all items", model == m)
iper <- \(s) paste(irel(s, "Rasch", n_runs), "runs")
iit  <- \(s) as.character(irel(s, "Rasch", n_items))
n_model <- paste(res_rel$meta$n_items_analysis, "in model")
drel <- \(s) pick(res_dim$irt_ld, rxx_uni, family == "guess", sample == s)
dn   <- \(s, col) pick(res_dim$samples, {{ col }}, sample == s)
rrel <- \(d, f) pick(res_rel$rel_by_form, rel_empirical, dataset == d, form == f)
rn   <- \(d, f) pick(res_rel$rel_by_form, n_runs, dataset == d, form == f)
rel_rec <- tribble(
  ~form, ~analysis, ~model, ~persons, ~items, ~reliability,
  "Leipzig item bank", "items & controls", "Rasch + g, single group, production priors", iper(de_s), iit(de_s), irel(de_s, "Rasch"),
  "Leipzig item bank", "items & controls", "2PL + g, single group, production priors", iper(de_s), iit(de_s), irel(de_s, "2PL"),
  "Leipzig item bank", "dimensionality", "2PL + g, single group, slope prior N(0, 2²)", paste(dn("de_ib", children), "children (first run)"), as.character(dn("de_ib", items)), drel("de_ib"),
  "Leipzig item bank", "reliability", "2PL + g, 8-group concurrent calibration", paste(rn("pilot_mpieva_de_main", "item_bank"), "runs"), n_model, rrel("pilot_mpieva_de_main", "item_bank"),
  "Western item bank", "dimensionality", "2PL + g, single group, slope prior N(0, 2²)", paste(dn("wca_ib", children), "children"), as.character(dn("wca_ib", items)), drel("wca_ib"),
  "Western item bank", "reliability", "2PL + g, 8-group concurrent calibration", paste(rn("pilot_western_ca_main", "item_bank"), "runs"), n_model, rrel("pilot_western_ca_main", "item_bank"),
  "Bogotá item bank", "dimensionality", "2PL + g, single group, slope prior N(0, 2²)", paste(dn("bog_ib", children), "children"), as.character(dn("bog_ib", items)), drel("bog_ib"),
  "Bogotá item bank", "reliability", "2PL + g, 8-group concurrent calibration", paste(rn("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota", "item_bank"), "runs"), n_model, rrel("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota", "item_bank"),
  "UTDT no-HA retest-B", "items & controls", "Rasch + g, UTDT-AR main only", iper(ar_s), iit(ar_s), irel(ar_s, "Rasch"),
  "UTDT no-HA retest-B", "items & controls", "2PL + g, UTDT-AR main only", iper(ar_s), iit(ar_s), irel(ar_s, "2PL"),
  "UTDT no-HA retest-B", "dimensionality", "2PL + g, UTDT-AR main + UTDT-intl pooled", paste(dn("ar_nhb", children), "children"), as.character(dn("ar_nhb", items)), drel("ar_nhb"),
  "UTDT no-HA retest-B", "reliability", "2PL + g, 8-group; UTDT-AR main", paste(rn("rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "no_ha_retest_B"), "runs"), n_model, rrel("rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "no_ha_retest_B"),
  "UTDT no-HA retest-B", "reliability", "2PL + g, 8-group; UTDT-intl", paste(rn("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", "no_ha_retest_B"), "runs"), n_model, rrel("rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", "no_ha_retest_B")
)
rel_rec |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Empirical (EAP) reliability of the same fixed forms in the three analyses")
```

For these four forms the estimates differ by up to
`r n2(max(tapply(rel_rec$reliability, rel_rec$form, \(x) diff(range(x)))))`
between analyses and range over `r rng(rel_rec$reliability)`. Across all
single fixed forms with at least 25 runs the range is wider
(`r k$rel_forms`, table above); the lowest are Leipzig's retest forms,
taken by a near-ceiling sample. Pooling a dataset's fixed forms gives
`r k$rel_fixed`. On every version of the number, a fixed Stories form
is far from a .9 instrument. The differences between analyses have ordinary
causes, though none was tested separately:

- The dimensionality fits use a weak slope prior within one sample and drop
  near-ceiling items. The reliability model shares item parameters across 8
  groups and shrinks slopes toward 1.
- The dimensionality es-AR sample pools two UTDT datasets whose means
  differ by about
  `r n2(pick(res_rel$group_pars, mean_analysis, dataset == "rfp1_utdt_ar_main") - pick(res_rel$group_pars, mean_analysis, dataset == "rfp1_utdt_intl_ys"), 1)`
  logits in the reliability model
  (`r n2(pick(res_rel$group_pars, mean_analysis, dataset == "rfp1_utdt_ar_main"))`
  vs `r n2(pick(res_rel$group_pars, mean_analysis, dataset == "rfp1_utdt_intl_ys"))`;
  the UTDT-intl mean pools its fCAT and fixed-form runs). The pooling widens
  the ability distribution, which raises reliability.

```{r june-equiv}
res_rel$june_equivalents |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "June-comparable quantities on the corrected model")
res_dim$june_pool_check |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "June's '.92 reliable composite', recomputed with June's method on the Leipzig pool")
```

June's ".92" is the Rasch marginal reliability of the whole pooled Leipzig
item set: `r jp$items_in_model` items across forms, of which children
answered a median of `r jp$items_per_run_median`. It reproduces
(`r n2(jp$rasch_marginal_rxx_june_method, 3)`), but the same model's
reliability for the items children actually answered is
`r n2(jp$rasch_empirical_rxx_eap, 3)`. On the corrected 2PL model, the
full-bank marginal reliability for DE is `r n2(k$de_bank, 3)`. No child
takes the full bank.

## Stability (Leipzig)

Only Leipzig has repeated ToM runs in any number. They are different forms,
months apart, so the numbers below are alternate-form stability, not
test–retest reliability. Only
`r pick(res_rel$stability_forms, n_pairs, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[0,60)")`
pairs are less than 60 days apart.

```{r stability}
res_rel$stability_bins |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main") |>
  transmute(gap_bin, version, n_pairs, median_gap_days, r, r_lo, r_hi, r_partial_age,
            r_disattenuated, diff_vs_released, diff_lo, diff_hi) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Leipzig alternate-form stability by gap (bootstrap 95% CIs, 2,000 resamples of pairs)")
res_rel$stability_first2 |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main") |>
  select(-dataset) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "First two runs per child (Leipzig)")
res_rel$stability_forms |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", !is.na(r)) |>
  select(-dataset) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "By form pair")
```

```{r stab-numbers}
sf2 <- res_rel$stability_first2 |> filter(dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main")
```

Stability is
`r n2(pick(sb, r, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[60,180)", version == "analysis"))`
at 60–180 days,
`r n2(pick(sb, r, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[180,300)", version == "analysis"))`
at 180–300 days and
`r n2(pick(sb, r, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[300,Inf)", version == "analysis"))`
beyond 300 days. Disattenuated for measurement error it is
`r n2(pick(sb, r_disattenuated, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", gap_bin == "[60,180)", version == "analysis"))`
at 60–180 days, so most of the instability is measurement error. The
corrections do not raise it: over the first two runs it is
`r n2(pick(sf2, r, version == "analysis"), 3)`, against
`r n2(pick(sf2, r, version == "released v2_3"), 3)` for the released scores
and `r n2(pick(sf2, r, version == "release-equivalent refit"), 3)` for
the same model refitted on release-equivalent data. June reported that its
fix raised stability from about .45 to .53; on these data the corrections
lower it slightly, within noise. The small 60–180-day difference from the
released scores appears already in the "identity fixes only" rows (PR #27's
identity fixes and restored trials), not with the item exclusions; which of
those fixes produces it was not examined.

de_av_fcat <- pick(res_rel$age_validity, r_age, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main", form == "fCAT")

Age validity within a dataset ranges from weak to moderate (r =
`r rng(av$r_age)`; the weakest is `r ds_label(av$dataset[which.min(av$r_age)])`). How
large it is mostly tracks each sample's age range: the SD of age is
`r rng(av$age_sd[str_starts(av$dataset, "pilot")], 1)` years in the pilot

`r rng(av$slope_per_year[av$dataset != "pilot_mpieva_de_main"])` logits
outside Leipzig, and
`r n2(pick(av, slope_per_year, dataset == "pilot_mpieva_de_main"))` in

(`r n2(de_av_fcat)`). The corrections barely change age validity (compare
`r_age_released`).
