## What changes from the released scores

```{r released}
res_rel$released_comparison |>
  left_join(res_rel$released_models |> select(dataset, own_group_in_v2_3), by = "dataset") |>
  filter(!dataset %in% small_groups) |>
  transmute(dataset = ds_label(dataset), own_group_in_v2_3, n_runs,
            r_analysis_released, shift_analysis_minus_released,
            shift_refit_minus_released, shift_own_minus_ref_prior, shift_wide_minus_default_grid,
            shift_idfix_minus_refit, shift_analysis_minus_idfix) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Analysis EAP vs released v2_3 scores. The shift_* columns split the change: recalibration + own prior + grid (refit), the prior alone and the grid alone (items fixed), PR #27 (idfix), and policy exclusions (analysis minus idfix).")
res_rel$group_pars |>
  filter(!dataset %in% small_groups) |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Group means and variances (DE = N(0, 1)) under each model variant, and in v2_3")
```

```{r fig-released, fig.height=6}
res_rel$scores_plot |>
  filter(!dataset %in% small_groups, !is.na(score_released)) |>
  mutate(dataset = ds_label(dataset)) |>
  ggplot(aes(score_released, eap)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = .6, alpha = .3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset), nrow = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  labs(x = "Released v2_3 score", y = "Analysis EAP", title = "Analysis scores vs released scores (dashed: y = x)") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10))
```

- Rank order within a dataset is largely preserved (r =
  `r rng(rc$r_analysis_released, 3)`), but not unchanged.
- The four datasets that had their own group in v2_3 keep their level
  (shifts `r rng(rc$shift_analysis_minus_released[rc$dataset %in% own])`).
  The datasets v2_3 scored under the German prior drop by
  `r k$shift_total` logits in total (recalibration, own prior, wider grid
  and data corrections together). Scored under their own prior instead of
  the German one, with the items held fixed, they drop by `r k$shift_prior`
  logits, so the prior accounts for most of the change. As the reliability
  section shows, these low-scoring groups' levels are themselves weakly
  identified.
- The data corrections move dataset means little, except in Bogotá. There,
  dropping the policy-flagged items (mainly the V0 2e reality check, but
  also reference_reference) raises the mean by
  `r n2(pick(rc, shift_analysis_minus_idfix, dataset == "pilot_uniandes_co_bogota"))`.
- Group means assume scalar invariance, which does not hold, and they are
  confounded with age. They are not cross-cultural comparisons. In
  Bogotá, UTDT-intl and MPIB-intl,
  `r pct(min(res_rel$rel_by_form$prop_at_or_below_guessing[res_rel$rel_by_form$form == "all forms" & res_rel$rel_by_form$dataset %in% c("rfp1_mpib_intl_ys", "rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", "pilot_uniandes_co_bogota")]))`–`r pct(max(res_rel$rel_by_form$prop_at_or_below_guessing[res_rel$rel_by_form$form == "all forms" & res_rel$rel_by_form$dataset %in% c("rfp1_mpib_intl_ys", "rfp1_utdt_intl_ys", "pilot_uniandes_co_bogota")]))`
  of runs score at or below what guessing would give, so for those children
  the EAP rests largely on the prior.

# Designing the block CAT

```{r cat-setup}
val <- res_cat$validation$fcat3_random
val_time <- res_cat$validation$time
q5m <- res_cat$q5 |> group_by(se_inflation, rule) |>
  summarise(across(c(capitalization, selection_loss, rescoring_gain), mean), .groups = "drop")
q4r <- res_cat$q4_two |> filter(growth == "latent_slope", !history_aware) |>
  group_by(design, rule, gap_years) |> summarise(repeated = mean(share_repeated), .groups = "drop")
q4cost <- res_cat$q4_two |> filter(growth == "latent_slope") |>
  select(dataset, design, rule, gap_years, history_aware, rel_wave2) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = history_aware, values_from = rel_wave2, names_prefix = "ha_") |>
  group_by(design, rule, gap_years) |> summarise(cost = mean(ha_FALSE - ha_TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

The deployed fCAT picks one story at random from each of three blocks. To decide how a real block CAT should choose stories, we simulated administrations from the analysis model (`tasks/_stories_cat_sim.R`).

**The simulation.**

- **Items:** the analysis model's items, minus story 4's reality checks 2 and 3 (broken on image 4g). Their time is still counted: `r length(res_cat$meta$bank_items)` items.
- **Children:** each calibration group's latent distribution, with `r big(res_cat$meta$n[["main"]])` simulated children per group and design.
- **Time:** story durations from the deployed fCAT runs, with a per-child speed effect.
- **Procedure:** after each story, ability is updated by EAP under the group's prior, and the next story is chosen within its block.
- **Validation:** the simulated deployed design matches the observed fCAT. Reliability agrees within `r n2(max(abs(val$sim_rel_fcat3_random - val$obs_rel_group_fcat), na.rm = TRUE))` per dataset, and the median time is `r n2(median(val$sim_median_min), 1)` min simulated vs `r n2(val_time$obs_median_min, 1)` observed. The 90th-percentile time is `r n2(val_time$obs_q90_min - median(val$sim_q90_min), 1)` min too short, so read every 90th-percentile figure below as that much optimistic.

This is a model-based simulation. It assumes the 2PL with fixed guessing holds, with scalar invariance except where tested below, and it models no practice effects.

## Precision against time

```{r cat-grid}
cat_grid |>
  filter(rule %in% c("random", "maxinfo", "infomin", "rq2", "fixed")) |>
  mutate(rule = factor(rule_labels[rule], unname(rule_labels))) |>
  select(design, n_stories, rule, rel) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = rel) |>
  left_join(cat_grid |> filter(rule %in% c("maxinfo", "fixed")) |>
              transmute(design, minutes = paste0(n2(med_min, 1), " / ", n2(q90_min, 1))),
            by = "design") |>
  left_join(cat_designs |> select(design, design_label, steps), by = "design") |>
  arrange(n_stories, match(design, c("cur3", "canvas3", "best3", "free3", "cur3p1", "canvas4",
                                     "best4", "free4", "fixed_1to6", "fixed_13to18"))) |>
  select(-design) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double) & !n_stories, \(x) if_else(is.na(x), "", n2(x))),
         n_stories = as.integer(n_stories)) |>
  select(design = design_label, blocks = steps, stories = n_stories,
         any_of(unname(rule_labels[c("random", "maxinfo", "infomin", "rq2", "fixed")])), minutes) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Mean reliability over the 8 groups by design and selection rule;",
                               "minutes = median / 90th percentile under max information",
                               "(fixed forms: the whole form). RK reality known, IN interpretation,",
                               "MR moral reasoning, SO second order, DC deception, RF reference."))
```

```{r cat-grid-plot, fig.height = 4.5}
cat_grid |>
  filter(rule %in% c("random", "maxinfo", "rq2", "fixed")) |>
  left_join(cat_designs |> select(design, design_label), by = "design") |>
  ggplot(aes(med_min, rel, colour = rule_labels[rule], shape = factor(n_stories))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = design), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Median minutes", y = "Mean reliability (8 groups)", colour = "Selection", shape = "Stories") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- **Adaptive selection within today's blocks is the largest single gain.** Reliability goes from `r n2(cg("cur3", "random"))` to `r n2(cg("cur3", "maxinfo"))` in the same time (`r n2(cg("cur3", "random", "med_min"), 1)` vs `r n2(cg("cur3", "maxinfo", "med_min"), 1)` median minutes).
- **A fourth story adds about as much again.** The current three blocks plus one free story (at most one per story type) reach `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo"))` in `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo", "med_min"), 1)` median minutes. That beats a fixed six-story form (`r n2(cg("fixed_1to6", "fixed"))`, `r n2(cg("fixed_1to6", "fixed", "med_min"), 1)` min) in about 2.5 fewer minutes.
- **Grouping matters less than selection.**
  - The searched 4-block grouping splits today's moral-reasoning + second-order block into two single-type blocks: `r n2(cg("best4", "maxinfo"))`.
  - No blocks at all, with at most one story per type: `r n2(cg("free4", "maxinfo"))`.
  - The canvas 4-block design: `r n2(cg("canvas4", "maxinfo"))`, lower because every child must take a two-question reality-known story.

```{r cat-by-group}
res_cat$q1 |>
  filter((design == "cur3" & rule %in% c("random", "maxinfo")) |
         (design %in% c("cur3p1", "canvas4", "best4") & rule == "maxinfo") |
         (design == "fixed_1to6" & rule == "fixed")) |>
  mutate(cell = paste(design, rule_labels[rule], sep = ", ")) |>
  select(label, cell, rel_realized) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = rel_realized) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) n2(x))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Reliability by group for the main designs")
```

```{r cat-blocks}
res_cat$block_balance |>
  filter(design %in% c("cur3", "canvas4", "best4")) |>
  transmute(design, block, stories, types, `expected info, best story` = n2(exp_info_best),
            `expected info, mean story` = n2(exp_info_mean), `median seconds` = median_secs_range) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Information and time per block (expected information averaged over the groups)")
```

Today's blocks are unbalanced. The moral-reasoning + second-order block carries about twice the information of the reality-known + interpretation block. The canvas design's reality-known block (stories 1, 7 and 13: two questions each, about 40 seconds) carries the least.

## Choosing stories: information, not discrimination

```{r cat-disc}
res_cat$disc_vs_info_cor |>
  transmute(theta, `rank r, summed discrimination vs information` = n2(spearman_sum_a2),
            `best story` = best_story_info, `highest-discrimination story` = best_story_sum_a2,
            `its share of the best story's information` = pct(info_ratio_top_a2_to_best)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Does a story's discrimination predict its information at a given ability?")
```

Choosing the story with the highest summed discrimination gives `r n2(cg("cur3", "disc_a2"))` against `r n2(cg("cur3", "maxinfo"))` for information-based selection in today's blocks (mean over groups). It does as well as information-based selection for the higher-scoring groups (Leipzig, Sheffield, Western), but for the lowest-scoring samples it is no better than random: `r dq <- res_cat$q1 |> filter(design == "cur3", rule %in% c("random", "disc_a2"), label %in% c("MPIB-intl", "UTDT-intl", "Bogota")) |> select(label, rule, rel_realized) |> pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = rel_realized); paste0(dq$label, " ", n2(dq$disc_a2), " vs ", n2(dq$random), " random", collapse = "; ")`. Discrimination tracks information only near the middle of the scale. Where most young Spanish-speaking children sit, the high-discrimination stories are pitched too hard: story 14 has the highest summed discrimination, while story 18 carries most of the information below θ = −2. What to maximize is each story's Fisher information at the child's current EAP, summed over its questions. Dividing by expected minutes (information per minute) gives about the same reliability in slightly less time.

## Starting value and prior

```{r cat-start}
res_cat$q3 |>
  filter(rule == "maxinfo", design %in% c("cur3", "best4")) |>
  group_by(design, start) |> summarise(rel = mean(rel_realized), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(start = recode(start, zero = "θ = 0, group prior", group_mean = "group mean",
                        age = "age-predicted", zero_refprior = "θ = 0 under the N(0, 1) reference prior",
                        pooled_prior = "pooled 8-group prior"),
         rel = n2(rel)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = design, values_from = rel) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean reliability by starting value and the prior used while testing (max information)")
```

Start each child at the group mean, or at an age-predicted value, which gives more variety in the first story. Run the online estimate under the group's prior. Running the whole test under the German N(0, 1) reference prior is the one choice that hurts badly, and it hurts most in the lowest-scoring groups. For a site without its own calibration, the pooled prior is a reasonable fallback, followed by rescoring once the site's own distribution is known.

## Retest: repeated stories

```{r cat-retest}
q4r |>
  filter(gap_years == 1, design %in% c("cur3", "canvas4", "best4", "free4")) |>
  left_join(q4cost |> filter(gap_years == 1), by = c("design", "rule", "gap_years")) |>
  transmute(design, rule = rule_labels[rule], `stories repeated at 12 months` = pct(repeated),
            `reliability cost of forbidding repeats` = n2(abs(round(cost, 3)), 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Second wave 12 months later, with growth from the data (latent slopes)")
res_cat$q4_waves_bound |> rename(`waves without any repeat` = bound) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "How many waves each grouping allows before a story must repeat")
```

Pure information-based selection gives most children the same stories at every wave, because growth of a few tenths of a logit a year barely changes the best story. Choosing at random among the top two about halves the repeats, at little cost. Forbidding repeats costs reliability at every wave. Across six history-aware waves, reliability in the current three blocks falls below random selection by wave 4, because the informative stories are used up. Whether re-seeing a story causes a practice effect is not in these data; only a retest study can answer that.

## Calibration error and rescoring after the fact

```{r cat-calib}
q5m |>
  transmute(`calibration SEs` = if_else(se_inflation == 1, "current", "doubled"),
            rule = rule_labels[rule],
            `overstated reliability (capitalization)` = n2(capitalization, 3),
            `lost to worse story choices` = n2(selection_loss, 3),
            `recovered by rescoring with true parameters` = n2(rescoring_gain, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Selecting with perturbed parameters, scoring with the true ones (mean over groups and designs)")
```

At today's calibration precision, runtime parameter error barely matters. Rescoring after the fact recovers the scoring error, but it cannot change which stories were given; with doubled SEs (a new language on a small calibration sample), that loss is about .01. Recalibrating before deployment on the corrected data is still worthwhile. Rescoring every administration offline, as the score of record, is what makes the runtime parameters low-stakes.

## Cross-language non-invariance

```{r cat-dif}
res_cat$q6 |>
  filter(rule == "maxinfo", design %in% c("cur3", "best4")) |>
  group_by(label, language, variant, design) |>
  summarise(across(c(bias_pooled, bias_rescored, realized_pooled, realized_rescored, realized_oracle), mean),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) n2(x))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Responses generated with group-specific difficulties, stories selected with pooled",
                               "parameters; bias (logits) and realized reliability, scored with pooled vs",
                               "group-specific parameters. Variants bracket the two items at the guessing floor."))
```

The pooled parameters for stories 13–18 are dominated by Argentine data, so under non-invariance it is the German children who are scored off-model on those stories, not the Argentine ones. Rescoring with group-specific parameters removes the bias. This also flags a caveat for this chapter's German scores on stories 13–18.

## Local dependence

Generating responses with story testlet effects, but selecting and scoring with the unidimensional model, overstates reliability by `r n2(min(res_cat$q7 |> filter(rule == "maxinfo", scenario != "independent") |> group_by(scenario) |> summarise(o = mean(predicted - realized)) |> pull(o)), 3)`–`r n2(max(res_cat$q7 |> filter(rule == "maxinfo", scenario != "independent") |> group_by(scenario) |> summarise(o = mean(predicted - realized)) |> pull(o)), 3)`. The ranking of designs is unchanged (rank r ≥ `r n2(min(res_cat$q7_rank$spearman_pred_real))`). A testlet model is not needed for selection. Discount reliability claims slightly.

## Recommendation

1. **Select stories adaptively within blocks,** by Fisher information at the current EAP (or information per minute), not by discrimination.
2. **Give 4 stories:** today's three blocks plus one free story, at most one per story type. That is about `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo", "med_min"), 1)` minutes median and about `r n2(cg("cur3p1", "maxinfo", "q90_min") + val_time$obs_q90_min - median(val$sim_q90_min), 1)` at the 90th percentile (adding the simulation's known shortfall). It ties the best 4-block grouping, is the smallest change from today, and allows the most waves before stories must repeat. It is also better than the canvas grouping.
3. **Start at the group mean or an age-predicted value, and run the online estimate under the group's prior.** For new sites, use the pooled prior and rescore afterwards. Never test under N(0, 1).
4. **Use top-2 randomesque selection,** at least until recalibration. It spreads exposure and calibration data across stories and halves repeats at retest. Allow repeats rather than forbidding them until a retest study measures practice effects.
5. **Before deploying:**
   - recalibrate on the corrected data (after levantemodels PR #27);
   - fix or remove the dead items;
   - rescore every administration offline as the score of record, group by group, with group-specific parameters for items known to be non-invariant.
6. **Engineering:**
   - core-tasks needs story-level selection;
   - the runtime ability update must use each item's discrimination (today it is fixed at 1);
   - estimation must be EAP with a prior;
   - θ, SE and the chosen story should be logged per trial.

   The item bank is thin above θ = 0 on the German scale, so better precision for older or higher-scoring children needs harder stories as well as a better selection rule.

# June conclusions → now

Each June conclusion is re-tested on the corrected data and labelled by
these criteria:

- **survives**: same direction and same practical conclusion, with an
  estimate close to June's;
- **survives with changes**: same conclusion, but a materially different
  magnitude or a narrower scope;
- **partly overturned**: the conclusion holds in some samples, models or
  designs and fails in others;
- **different mechanism**: June's number is reproduced, but by a different
  route than June described;
- **not replicated**: June's estimate is not reproduced on these data;
- **overturned**: the conclusion is contradicted;
- **not re-tested**.

```{r june-table}
  glue("{big(round(jbv('J_release', 'all', X2)))} → {big(round(jbv('J_policy', 'all', X2)))} ({spct(jbv('J_policy', 'all', X2_change_vs_release))}); controls {spct(jbv('J_policy', 'controls', X2_change_vs_release))}; PR #27 alone {spct(jbv('J_corrected', 'all', X2_change_vs_release))}"),
  "different mechanism (about half, from exclusions, not key flips)",

  "tom_reality_check_bug; README", "The 12 hand-flagged items are essentially a complete catalog of defects",
  "all 12 map onto defects",
  glue("{k$v_un} of {k$v_all} story-level items un-excluded; {k$v_keep} keep; {k$v_scop} scoped; {k$v_es} held for the translation check"),
  "overturned",

  "stories_tom §1", "Fixing the scoring bug raised Leipzig test–retest",
  "≈ .45 → ≈ .53",
  glue("first two runs {n2(pick(sf2, r, version == 'analysis'), 3)} (released {n2(pick(sf2, r, version == 'released v2_3'), 3)}; release-equivalent refit {n2(pick(sf2, r, version == 'release-equivalent refit'), 3)}); 60–180 d {n2(k$stab_60)}; > 300 d {n2(pick(sb, r, dataset == 'pilot_mpieva_de_main', gap_bin == '[300,Inf)', version == 'analysis'))}"),
  "not replicated (the corrections do not raise it; alternate forms, months apart)",

  "stories_tom §6", "Parallel retest items are broadly similar in difficulty",
  "within-family SD ≈ 0.9 vs 2.3",
  "not re-tested",
  "not re-tested"
)
knitr::kable(jt, col.names = c("June source", "Claim", "June (quoted)", "Now (2026-09 data)", "Status"))
```

# Synthesis and recommendations

```{r rec-numbers}
fb_flag <- res_inv$dif |>
  filter(analysis %in% c("A", "B"), question_type == "false_belief", class != "A") |>
  mutate(story = as.integer(str_extract(short, "(?<=story)\\d+"))) |>
  arrange(story) |> pull(short) |> unique()
k$fb_flag_list <- paste(uid_label(fb_flag), collapse = ", ")
```

**Exclusions and corrections (DCC).**

1. Keep item exclusions in the Airtable table, as the DCC prefers, but
   fix what is there. The 12 generic rows do nothing today (the `anti_join`
   runs after `recode_tom()`), and they would over-exclude if they worked.
   Replace them with story-level rows: un-exclude the `r k$v_un` story-level
   items that behave normally (`r k$v_weak` of them weak); exclude
   reference_reference in stories 5/11/17 and story 10's deception false
   belief 1 everywhere; and add the three content-scoped rows above, which
   need a content-version (or date-window) column. Hold any Spanish row for
   story 13 until the translation check.
2. The same reasoning applies to corrections. PR #27 writes its identity
   remaps (`fix_tom_item_uids()`: a 25-row table keyed on date window, item
   code, answer and occurrence) and three per-story chance values into
   levantemodels code. Those are data properties too. A metadata table, such
   as the item-mapping tables in `levante_metadata_items`, would document
   them next to the exclusions, and could also hold a scoped key correction
   for the story-4 reality checks on image 4g if the content team confirms
   that "no" is right for that scene (that would keep
   `r big(sum(res_items$flip_check$n[res_items$flip_check$content_part == "flagged: 4g" & res_items$flip_check$language == "all"]))`
   trials). This is a design choice for the DCC; the analysis only needs the
   corrections applied somewhere.
3. Consider V0 Bogotá story-2 reality check 2 and story 5's reference
   reality check (non-invariant only because of V0) as further V0-scoped
   rows, next to V0 reality check 1, whose cause stays undetermined.

**Deployed items (core-tasks; item bank).**

4. Re-author story-4 reality checks 2/3 for image 4g (or change their key,
   as above), and redesign reference_reference (stories 5/11/17). Both are
   still in the deployed corpora.
5. Review the near-chance yes/no "Is [sibling] mad at [sibling]?" questions
   (story 4 fb_3, story 16 ref_2), the non-discriminating story-17 emotion
   question and story 10's deception false belief 1, and the same-scene
   doublets (story 6 fb_2/fb_5, both keyed "shoes"; story 4 fb_2/fb_3, both
   "no").
6. Check the Spanish translations (es-CO, es-AR) of the false-belief
   prompts: every false-belief item flagged (class B or C) in the invariance
   analyses (`r k$fb_flag_list`), plus story 7's reality_known item, which
   the item screen flags (stories 7–12 are in no invariance analysis).
   Translation is one hypothesis; prior exposure to the task and the samples
   themselves are others. (Sites that share a language differ less and on
   other items, and the false-belief DIF persists with younger German
   children, so site and age alone do not explain it.) Until the check is done,
   keep the Spanish sensitivity flag and report results with and without
   it; it changes scores very little.

**Scoring.**

7. Score group by group (the PR #26 rule, not yet merged). Before changing
   production's integration grid, investigate how the low-scoring groups'
   means and variances depend on the grid, the latent density and the
   guessing convention: all three move them, while scores within a group
   barely change. For the RfP1 datasets that v2_3 scored under the German
   prior, their own prior alone lowers the level by `r k$shift_prior`
   logits (`r k$shift_total` in total).
8. Recalibrate ToM on the current data once PR #27 is merged. The analysis
   model here uses `r big(pick(res_rel$itemtype_bic, runs, model == "analysis", itemtype == "2PL"))`
   runs in 8 groups. The 2PL is preferred, and local dependence is modest,
   so a testlet model is optional. If it is skipped, discount story
   information by about `r k$info_over` in reliability claims. The block-CAT
   simulation shows it does not change which stories are selected.
9. Treat cross-language comparisons of Stories scores as partial-scalar at
   best, and remember that the language groups also differ in age, prior
   exposure and site. Report group differences only with that caveat and
   adjusted for age.

**Block CAT and the item bank.**

10. The deployed fCAT is a random 3-story form with reliability
    `r k$rel_fcat` in a median of `r k$fcat_min` minutes. In the same
    children, three random stories instead of a six-story form cost
    `r rng(cs$rel_full - cs$rel_random)` in reliability for half the time.
    The 3-vs-4 decision is mostly a trade of minutes for precision; the
    simulation in [Designing the block CAT](#designing-the-block-cat) recommends
    4 stories (today's blocks plus one free story) with adaptive selection.
11. Adaptive selection within blocks helps: choosing the more informative of
    the form's two stories per block raises the reliability of a 3-story
    form by a median of `r n2(median(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random))`
    (up to `r n2(max(cs$rel_adaptive - cs$rel_random))`) in the same time. With six stories per block it does more (simulation: `r n2(cg("cur3", "random"))` → `r n2(cg("cur3", "maxinfo"))`), but the bank is thin
    above θ = 0 on the DE scale, so real gains also need harder stories and
    items, calibrated in several languages. The fCAT's fixed block order
    confounds block with position; randomize it if blocks are to be
    compared.
12. The block structure need not follow the story constructs, which do not
    organize the item covariance. Question type's tetrachoric clustering
    partly reflects shared difficulty; once difficulty and guessing are
    modelled, what remains is weak and uneven across samples. Blocks can be
    chosen for content coverage and time.
13. Keep scoring the controls. If time binds, they are the least informative
    questions per item. Whether to keep administering them as comprehension
    checks is a design decision; the data show that a failed control makes
    the story's targets less age-informative mainly in Leipzig (and to a
    lesser degree in en-US), not in es-CO.
14. Only Leipzig has repeat data, as alternate forms months apart. A
    short-interval retest (same or parallel forms, about 2 weeks) at a
    high-volume site would give the first real test–retest estimate.

# Methods notes and caveats

- **Post-hoc rules.** Two rules in the items analysis were revised after
  its first run and are disclosed in `res_items$meta$notes`: the weak-item
  flag and the age-slope minority rule. The originals are kept in
  `r_ir_below_10` and `age_slope_raw`. The 2026-09 revision added, after
  review: the floor-corrected age slopes with a symmetric filter, the
  flipped-key check, the per-language discrimination rule for the Spanish
  items, story 10's deception false belief 1 as a policy exclusion, the
  within-language and age-restricted invariance variants, the 2PL tests,
  the latent-density check and the block-CAT simulation.
- **Guessing floor.** The reliability and invariance models fix it at
  chance; the dimensionality models set it to 0 for items answered at or
  below chance in the sample. The invariance and reliability conclusions
  were rechecked under the dimensionality rule (A_g0/B_g0 and the g0
  sensitivity of the reliability model). Neither rule
  can represent a group that answers systematically below chance, as young
  children do on reality_known false-belief questions.
- **`mirt::marginal_rxx()`** integrates TI/(TI + var) over N(0, 1) and
  assumes every item in the matrix is answered. The June chapters' ".92",
  ".89" and ".84" come from it on sparse, multi-form matrices. This chapter
  reports empirical reliability instead.
- **MAP, not ML.** The fixed-floor 2PL and bifactor fits in the
  dimensionality analysis use an N(0, 2²) slope prior, and the invariance
  2PL uses the production priors; their AIC and BIC are evaluated at MAP
  estimates. The bootstrap intervals for ev1/ev2 are biased downward, so the
  chapter reports a bootstrap SE instead of percentile intervals.
- **Upper bounds.** The reliabilities come from unidimensional models that
  assume scalar invariance, so they overstate precision somewhat (footnote
  in the reliability section).
- **Confounds.** Language, site, age, prior exposure, form and deployment
  epoch overlap. The es-AR samples are young
  (`r pick(res_dim$samples, age_min, sample == "ar_nhb")`–`r pick(res_dim$samples, age_max, sample == "ar_nhb")`
  years), the Leipzig samples are older, near ceiling and mostly on repeat
  runs in stories 13–18, and es-CO in the invariance analysis pools
  `r length(str_split_1(pick(res_inv$samples, datasets, analysis == "A", group == "es_CO"), ", "))`
  datasets from 2024–2026. The age-band plots describe; they are not a
  model-based age adjustment.
- **Coverage.** en-GB (Sheffield, fCAT only) has too few responses per item
  for the invariance analyses. en-US items from stories 7–18 have fewer
  than 30 responses. Stories 7–12 are sparse everywhere.
- **Gating** conditions on passing a control, which depends on ability, so
  it is descriptive.
- **Invariance fits** use mirt's default θ range (see the numerics note).
- **Not re-tested:** June's parallel-retest-family analysis (stories_tom §6).

# Reproducing {#reproducing}

The chapter reads only cached files in `data/stories_2026-09/` (gitignored)
and fits no models. To rebuild, run the scripts in the order below with
`Rscript` from a working directory **outside** the repo (the book's renv has
an `mgcv` binary that breaks mirt). Each script takes the book root as its
argument (else `STORIES_BOOK_ROOT`, else the directory above the script's
`tasks/` folder). The build must
come first; the four analysis scripts only read its output and can run in
any order after it.

```{r repro}
tribble(
  ~step, ~script, ~writes, ~built,
  1, "tasks/_build_stories_data.R", "stories_trials.rds, stories_runs.rds, reconciliation.rds, README.md (and, if missing, the pinned raw pulls, release snapshots and the v2_3 model record)", format(prov$built_at),
  2, "tasks/_stories_fits_items.R", "results_items.rds", format(res_items$meta$built_at),
  3, "tasks/_stories_fits_dimensionality.R", "results_dimensionality.rds",
  paste0(res_dim$meta$run_at, " (", round(as.numeric(difftime(as.POSIXct(res_dim$meta$finished_at), as.POSIXct(res_dim$meta$run_at), units = "mins")), 1), " min)"),
  4, "tasks/_stories_fits_invariance.R", "results_invariance.rds",
  paste0(res_inv$meta$created, " (", round(res_inv$meta$runtime_min, 1), " min)"),
  5, "tasks/_stories_fits_reliability.R", "results_reliability.rds, stories_scores_analysis.rds", format(res_rel$meta$built_at)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Scripts in run order, outputs and build times")
```

```bash
cd /some/dir/outside/the/repo
export LEVANTEMODELS_PATH=/path/to/levantemodels   # checkout of PR #27's branch
Rscript /path/to/levante-analysis/tasks/_build_stories_data.R /path/to/levante-analysis
Rscript /path/to/levante-analysis/tasks/_stories_fits_items.R /path/to/levante-analysis
Rscript /path/to/levante-analysis/tasks/_stories_fits_dimensionality.R /path/to/levante-analysis
STORIES_CORES=6 Rscript /path/to/levante-analysis/tasks/_stories_fits_invariance.R /path/to/levante-analysis
Rscript /path/to/levante-analysis/tasks/_stories_fits_reliability.R /path/to/levante-analysis
```

The data build and the reliability script load levantemodels from the PR #27
source tree with `pkgload::load_all()`. `LEVANTEMODELS_PATH` must point to a
checkout of branch `fix-tom-identity-corrections` (they stop if it is
unset). They record its commit
(`r substr(res_rel$meta$levantemodels[["commit"]], 1, 7)` for the reliability
run). Every results file's `meta` element records the inputs, thresholds,
package versions and `sessionInfo()`. The data build pins every raw dataset
version (table above); the release snapshots are pinned by processed version,
except Sheffield's unreleased next draft, which cannot be pinned.
